chapters.title: Chapter 1: Global Selection
paragraphs: [ Select the Apocalypse you’d like to challenge. ]
It was 2:17 PM on a Tuesday when it all happened.
"This is real..." Kai muttered as he looked at the message that had appeared in front of him.
There were already four monitors on his desk, so the appearance of a fifth "screen" caught him off guard, but he didn’t panic.
Well, as a cybersecurity ethicist who later worked as a systems engineer, his first instinct was to trace its source or understand how the system message worked.
After all, it wasn’t rendering on any of his physical displays.
It was projected directly onto his eyes, or perhaps, a hologram that only he could see.
’What kind of technology is this? Neural interface? I’m not hallucinating, am I?’Kai thought as he read the message once again.
[ Select the Apocalypse you’d like to challenge. ]
[ You have 15 minutes to decide. ]
[ You will have a random Apocalypse to challenge if you fail to select within the given time. ]
[ A.I. Rebellion ]
[ Alien Invasion ]
[ Demon Invasion ]
[ Deep Sea Awakening ]
[ Divine Judgment ]
[ Dragon Awakening ]
[ Fairy Realm Collision ]
[ Lycans versus Vampires ]
[ Magic War ]
[ Parasitic Evolution ]
[ Ragnarok ]
[ Zombie Outbreak ]
Then, Kai confirmed he wasn’t crazy. All around him, he noticed that people were already staring into empty space.
Many of his coworkers were stunned, and a few of them didn’t even take that long to read the message. Soon, they vanished on the spot after selecting something.
However, some of them couldn’t accept this so easily.
"What is this? Should we call the police?"
"Who would even choose an apocalypse?"
"Is this a prank?! You’re messing with my mental health! I’ll sue you!"
"Hahaha! Just shut up! This is good! No more work! Zombie Outbreak... Ragnarok or Alien Invasion! Zombies, of course! Here I come! Adios, my fellow workers!"
One of his co-workers didn’t hesitate, and just like that, he selected Zombie Outbreak, vanishing on the spot.
The teleportation was instant... There was no particle effect or fade effect whatsoever.
It was like he was never there in the first place!
Still, the man’s previous words made Kai realize that the man probably only had three options, unlike him!
After Kai exhaled, he felt more in control and focused. He had 13 minutes left to decide. That guy probably had a different time frame, so he had to choose quickly.

Around him, panic had spread after everyone realized it was real. But some people were strangely calm, even thrilled, but most, especially those with families waiting at home, were crying or frozen in fear.
That was normal in his opinion.
Unfortunately, Kai didn’t have the time to worry about them.

Using his remaining time, he checked the Zombie Outbreak that the guy had chosen just now. He seemed so confident choosing it, and he couldn’t help but feel curious if there was a description that said it was an easy mode or something.
Then, as soon as he focused on this option, he confirmed that there were some details about this choice.
[ Zombie Outbreak:
"The pathogen spreads. The dead rise with a hunger for the living. Society collapses through its sheer number. The greatest threat may not be the bitten, but the survivors turning on each other."]
’No mention of easy mode... Just flavor text.’Kai thought as he read. It wasn’t helpful. He already knew what a Zombie Apocalypse meant, so the real concern was the intensity of the outbreak.

Nonetheless, he knew that he couldn’t select this type of Apocalypse. It was simply too dangerous... Getting bitten or injured by a Zombie means that he could turn into one of them. That would be the end of it, no healing, no recovery.
The risk was too high. He couldn’t make a mistake in that scenario.
With that in mind, he checked the other Apocalypses...
Kai sighed as he shifted his focus to the next option that caught his attention. He didn’t really like the A.I. Rebellion, Alien Invasion, and Demon Invasion, so he turned to the next one.
[ Deep Sea Awakening:
"The oceans rise, swallowing coastlines and cities. Ancient creatures emerge from the abyss, claiming dominion over the drowned lands. Humanity must retreat inland or be consumed by the tide."]
Kai grimaced.
’Water... swimming... that’s a death sentence for me.’
He hated the ocean. Even the thought of being dragged under by currents or facing something massive from the deep made his chest tighten. "No way... This one’s suicide."
He had thought it was a different kind of awakening. Anyway, he turned to the next one.
[ Divine Judgment:
"The heavens open, and celestial wrath descends. Angels and divine beings purge the unworthy. Survival depends on faith, obedience, or defiance against the divine decree." ]

Kai frowned. "What the heck? Is this some kind of faith-based apocalypse? That’s not something I can gamble on. What if they decide I’m unworthy from the start? No chance to fight back, no chance to negotiate. Just judgment?" He shook his head. "Not for me."
Next was Dragon Awakening.
[ Dragon Awakening:
"The ancient beasts rise from their slumber...
Kai helplessly smiled as he continued reading... "Dragons... and we’re forced to live in the cave or something?"
He dismissed it immediately.
[ Fairy Realm Collision:
"The gate between worlds collapses. The fairy realm merges with reality, and mana starts leaking. Time flows unpredictably, and mystical beings of the other realm will claim the land." ]

’Fairy Realm merging with Earth? I think this is decent.’Kai thought. The only concern was the mystical beings that he might be facing there. After all, it was obvious that the humans would be the protectors of the Earth from these mystical beings. If these beings were something too overpowered, like Giants, Phoenix, or maybe even Ogres and Minotaurs, it would be at the lower end of his options... though fighting kobolds or goblins might be doable.
Then came Lycans versus Vampires.
[ Lycans versus Vampires:
"The night belongs to predators. Vampires and werewolves wage war across the land, dragging humanity into their conflict. Blood and moonlight dictate survival."]
"Being caught between two monsters fighting for dominance? Are we going to be recruited and choose sides or something?" Kai muttered.

Still, he believed that it would be the Lycans who would win against the Vampires after reading a long discussion online about them... If he somehow entered this realm, he’d definitely try siding with them.
He then checked Magic War.
[ Magic War:
"Mana floods the world. Sorcerers and warlocks clash, tearing reality apart with spells. Ordinary humans must adapt or perish in the crossfire."]
Kai stared at the message...
’Adapt, huh... Are we going to learn spells here and survive the war?’He mused. This might also be possible.
Next was Parasitic Evolution.
[ Parasitic Evolution:
"A new parasite spreads across all living beings. Hosts mutate, evolve, and turn against one another. Survival means resisting infection... or harnessing it."]
Kai shuddered. The last bit of this flavor text was definitely a warning.
"Parasites... no. Losing control of your own body? That’s worse than zombies. At least with zombies, you die. With parasites, you can live... but not as yourself."
Of course, he wasn’t exactly sure what would happen here, but he felt that a lot of betrayals could occur in this type of Apocalypse.
Ragnarok appeared next.
[ Ragnarok:
"The end of the gods. Mythic beasts, great giants, and divine warriors clash in a final war. Humanity is caught in the storm of prophecy."]
"That’s not even a fight I can join. That’s a war of gods. Humans are collateral damage. No thanks..." Kai muttered.
Anyone who would choose this apocalypse would be an idiot, followed by those who had selected Divine Judgment.
Having no other option, he glanced at the first selection... A.I. Rebellion.
[ A.I. Rebellion:
"Artificial intelligence gained more power and seized control... Machines rise against humanity, enforcing logic over life. Surveillance, drones, and mechanized armies hunt survivors."]
"A.I. Rebellion, huh... Machines rising against humanity." Kai muttered.
He just watched a movie about this, and although not as terrifying as other Apocalypses, it was still a difficult one, especially if they had already taken over most of the world.
He was about to shift his focus away when the screen blinked a few times...
"Hmm?"
[ Error... ]
[ Selection has been opted. ]
[ Challenge has been accepted. ]
[ Admin... ]
[ Error... ]
Kai froze. "What?!"
The text shifted again, and it was faster than he could react.
[ You have selected A.I. Rebellion. ]
[ Entering the Apocalypse... ]
[ You have entered the A.I. Rebellion: First Server... ]
[ Survivor Kai will enter a random starting region. ]
His heart skipped. "Oh shit... no! Why?! I still had time!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Choices
paragraphs: "No way..."
Kai was confused as he saw his surroundings turn white. He knew that he still had more than six minutes to decide!
However, for some reason, the system had glitched and forced him to select the last Apocalypse he had tried to check.
Unfortunately, he didn’t have the time to dwell on this as more system messages appeared.
[ Welcome to the Versailles Continent ]
[ The fate of the continent is in your hands! Survive and earn the title that is rightfully yours, and save your own world! ]
[ Every Survivor will awaken a Unique Talent to help you with your survival. ]
[ Finally, you can select one from the 10 Basic Gift Packs prepared by the Lord of the Realms before you begin. ]
[ You have 10 minutes to select. ]
[ Energy Gift Pack ]
[ Entertainment Gift Pack ]
[ Food Gift Pack ]
[ Medical Gift Pack ]
[ Shelter Gift Pack ]
[ Stealth Gift Pack ]
[ Survival Tools Gift Pack ]
[ Transport Gift Pack ]
[ Water Gift Pack ]
[ Weapon Gift Pack ]
Kai frowned at the sight of this new message.
"Versailles... unique talent... and gift packs. But only one? Out of ten? That’s... cruel." He clenched his fists as he knew that this would be a tough choice.

The system had already forced him into an apocalypse he hadn’t wanted, and now it was limiting his lifeline. He didn’t even know how he would start, whether he’d wake up in a ruined city, a forest, or a battlefield.
After all, he already realized the concept of this Apocalypse... It felt like the people of Earth were thrown into a game.
They were given choices and were transported to a different land depending on their chosen Apocalypse. It truly was like a game!
Then, Kai’s eyes lit up as he recalled the previous message that he would be at a random starting region.
’Right, a starting region. That must be the ’novice village’ or something...’ He mused. At the very least, it means that they should be a bit safe at the beginning stage of this Apocalypse.
He hoped so...
Still, he would be given a Unique Talent later. So he could only look forward to that.
After taking a deep breath, Kai began assessing each option carefully.

Thankfully, the system also provided information about their contents. The information wasn’t too specific in numbers and other details, but it was more than enough to get a general idea of what they could expect inside.
[ Energy Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: power bank, solar charger, batteries, and radio. ]
"Useful if I’m stuck somewhere with tech... but what if there’s no electricity at all? This feels too situational."
Obviously, no one would choose something like this.
[ Entertainment Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: playing cards, a journal, books, and a harmonica. ]
"Entertainment? In an apocalypse? Sure, mental health matters, but I’d rather not die with a harmonica in my hand." Kai scoffed at this content.
[ Food Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: canned goods, instant noodles, granola bars, tea bags, and mayonnaise. ]
Kai hesitated at this time. This was too important.
"Food is critical... but without water, this won’t last long. And mayonnaise? Who thought that was essential?"
[ Medical Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: first aid kit, painkillers, antibiotics, bandages. ]

Kai nodded slightly... He knew that this one was also a solid option. Injuries are inevitable, and having a first aid kit was definitely good. However, if they only had one choice, there was no way anyone would select it.
He then continued checking the others.
[ Shelter Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: small tent, sleeping bag, flashlight, thermal blanket, rain poncho. ]
[ Stealth Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: camouflage suit, night vision goggles, silencer, smoke grenade. ]
[ Survival Tools Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: fire starter, compass, pocket knife, whistle, rope, thermal blanket. ]
Kai felt a lot better after seeing these options.
"Now this... this could save my life."
He looked at the shelter or the stealth pack, and he knew that if he couldn’t fight, he could hide. But camouflage only works if the enemy relies on sight. What if the A.I. tracks heat or sound?
Kai then turned to the Survival Tools.
"Classic survival gear. They look reliable, but basic. This feels like something for camping, not an apocalypse. Still, it’s better than nothing."
He then turned to the next batch of Gift Packs.
[ Transport Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: folding bicycle, helmet, lock, and repair kit. ]
[ Water Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: water filter, filled bottles, purification tablets, collapsible bucket. ]
The contents of these two were simply too limited. Even if they were good, it felt wrong to select them.
After all, water could be collected from rain and other sources as long as his starting region wasn’t a desert.
Finally, he turned to the last.
[ Weapon Gift Pack (Basic)
Contents: revolver with six bullets, holster, extra ammo, hatchet. ]
Kai stared at the description. "Finally, something practical. But the extra ammo... I wonder how much there is. Once it’s gone, I’d be left with just the hatchet. A short-term solution, at best."

Kai couldn’t deny the gun’s usefulness. If he encountered other survivors who had chosen the same Apocalypse, conflict was inevitable. In countless scenarios, having such a weapon could make the difference
However, every pack has flaws.
"Tsk... Why do I only get one? One mistake here, and I’m dead before I even start."
The countdown ticked down.
Kai felt frustrated.
"Damn it. I don’t even know what kind of environment I’ll end up with. Choosing blind is the worst part."
If the timer runs out without him choosing any Gift Pack, he might not get anything at all!
So after a couple more minutes, Kai had to make a decision...
"I’ll choose you..."

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Apocalypse Event
paragraphs: Kai shifted his focus to the Survival Tool Gift Pack.
"I’ll choose you..."
[ You have selected the Survival Tool Gift Pack. ]
[ You can now receive your Talent. ]
Kai could only pray that he had made the right decision. After all, he didn’t know where he would end up.

The fire starter meant he could create warmth and cook food, if he could find them, without relying on luck. The pocket knife was small but dependable. It would be useful for cutting, carving, or defending himself in a pinch.
Rope and a compass offered flexibility for climbing, securing, or navigating unfamiliar terrain, while the whistle and thermal blanket could probably save his life in emergencies.
Compared to a pistol with limited ammunition, these tools were practical, reusable, and sustainable as long as he wasn’t forced into a battle as soon as he arrived in the starting region.
"Hmm?"
He then noticed the loading bar or progress bar appearing at the corner of his vision...
[ Beginning Survivor Analysis... ]
[ Scanning biological data... ]
[ Vital signs stable. ]
[ Neural activity detected. Cognitive adaptability: Above Average. ]
[ Emotional stability: Moderate. ]
[ Physical endurance: Low. ]
[ Risk assessment: High. ]
[ Cross-checking Apocalypse parameters... ]
[ Matching optimal Talent configuration... ]
Just like that, he felt as if the system had completely stripped him...
[ Analysis complete. ]
[ You have awakened your Survivor Talent! ]
[ You have equipped your Tier 1 Survivor Gear. ]
It didn’t say what talent he got, but Kai knew he would learn about it soon.
Kai let out a helpless smile. Everything was happening too fast. Even with all the books he’d read and the countless fantasy games he’d played, the reality before him still felt surreal.

Nonetheless, he knew that in this situation, he had to keep calm at all times. Especially if he couldn’t control the situation, it was something he had learned after being a systems engineer for years.
There was no point in reacting too much... this was already happening.
The next moment, his vision blurred. His body felt weightless, and before he could even take another breath, the white void around him collapsed.
"Ooomphh!"
When his sight returned, he was standing in a place that reeked of rot and decay.
"...A garbage dump?" Kai muttered.

Mountains of trash surrounded him... There was broken furniture, rusted metal, torn plastic bags, and piles of rotting food. The stench was overwhelming, forcing him to cover his nose with his sleeve.
"What the heck? Why throw me here?!"
This seemed to be one of the worst starting regions... or maybe not?
He then turned slowly, scanning the area. There was no one else. He was completely alone.
The sky above was dim and lifeless. There was no sun or any sight of blue sky at all. It was just a heavy gray blanket of cloud that made the world feel suffocated.
Kai looked down at himself and froze.
"Hmm?"
His office clothes were gone.

Instead, he was wearing rough, practical gear... It was a dark jacket, durable pants with six pockets, sturdy boots, and a belt with simple pouches. It wasn’t stylish, but it was clearly meant for survival.
"...Starter gear," he muttered. "So this is how it begins."
Kai clenched his fists as he forced himself to stay calm.
He wanted to take a deep breath, but the stench was overwhelming. Breathing too much of it would only make him sick.
As he looked around, the garbage dump stretched endlessly in every direction, and the silence was also quite unsettling.
He couldn’t even see the end of this garbage dump since there were mountains of trash blocking his sight.
Furthermore, there were no birds, no machines, no voices... just the faint rustle of trash shifting in the wind.
Kai exhaled slowly. "Alright... first step. Survive."
He already resigned himself to this new reality. With no family left behind on Earth, there was nothing to regret. Fear still gnawed at him, but he forced his thoughts into order.
As he accepted his new life, another message appeared.
[ Welcome, Survivor of the Versailles Continent! ]
[ As a beginner in this Apocalypse Event, you will have three days of Beginner Protection. Enemies will not appear in your area! ]
[ However, leaving your starting area will expire your Beginner Protection. ]
[ You can explore during these three days and plan your survival for the first week’s Mech Siege to get a reward! ]
[ Hint: You only need to survive during the Mech Siege in your area. You can either escape or fight them off, depending on your preference! ]
"Beginner protection, huh..." Kai gently nodded as he saw this message. Then, Kai noticed a digital timer in the corner of his vision. It confirmed the 3-day duration of the Protection.
Thankfully, the system or whoever brought them here wasn’t that cruel.
The Mech Siege was certainly concerning, but he felt that if he could hide well, there might be a chance of survival.
As for his goal here, it must be related to the previous message from the system... He recalled it clearly.
The fate of the continent is in your hands. Survive and earn the title that is rightfully yours, and save your own world.
’I have to survive and earn some title? Then save the world?’ He knew that it wasn’t as simple as that, but he would certainly do his best to survive.
’Wait... I still have that talent and gift pack. How to check that?’ Kai thought.
He then paused for a moment, wondering if there was some kind of command to bring up his information.
Then, just like in many games he had seen, he tried... "Status."
A faint chime rang in his ears, and a blue panel appeared before him.
[ Survivor Status ]
[ Name: Kai
Title: Beginner Survivor
Level: 1
Health: 100/100
Spirit: 50/50
Stamina 50/50
Talent: Weekly Gift Cycle (Rare)
Active Skills: None
Passive Skills: None
Inventory:
Survival Tool Gift Pack (Basic) x1 ]
"What kind of talent is this?" Kai muttered as he checked the Talent’s Description.
Just the name of it didn’t sound that great, but it could be an incredible talent.
"Let’s see..."

[ Weekly Gift Cycle (Rare): You can receive three Gift Packs every week. The packs will be delivered automatically at the start of each cycle, and you may freely choose which ones to claim. This talent ensures a steady supply of resources, giving you a consistent advantage in survival planning. ]
"Three gift packs every week? Seriously? But is this even good?" Kai certainly liked seeing that his talent was Rare. It’s better than Common or maybe Uncommon, after all.

However, he recalled the contents of the Gift Packs and surviving with only those things against the Mechs and the A.I. Overlords would be tough... It might be impossible unless he just continued hiding forever, since he would get some weekly supplies anyway.
Perhaps, if he finds a bunker or any hidden place, he could just live there silently and wait for this to be over.
’Living like that... no way.’Kai shook his head as he didn’t like this idea, although it sounded reasonable.
Then, before he could relax, the blue panel started blinking again... The letters distorted, breaking apart like corrupted code...
"What now?!"
[ Error... ]
[ Talent configuration mismatch. ]
[ Reassigning... ]
[ Error... ]
[ Override detected. ]
[ Talent Upgraded: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
Kai froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Limitation
paragraphs: Kai quickly checked the panel, his eyes focused on the Talent section.
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
’Triple S, huh.’Kai was filled with excitement. He knew in many games that the rarity SSS was definitely the best out there!
"Let’s see..." he muttered as he tapped the talent to see the description.

[ Infinite Gift Pack (SSS): You can claim an unlimited number of Gift Packs at any time. There are no restrictions on frequency, quantity, or type. This talent grants continuous access to supplies, ensuring that Gift Packs are always available whenever you choose to obtain them. ]
Kai was stunned. Although he already expected it, considering the name of the talent, he still felt shocked.
"Unlimited... Gift Packs?"
His heart raced as the words sank in. He could actually hear his heart beating loudly. This was a great talent in his opinion.
After all, he could obtain as many Gift Packs as he wanted. There were no cooldowns or any limits!
Well, there were no other effects like giving him more strength or some other flashy powers, but still... this was absurd.
A grin spread across his face.
"This is insane. Even if it doesn’t make me stronger directly, having unlimited supplies... that’s more than enough to survive."
He clenched his fists as he calmed himself.
Now, he would have endless food, tools, and gear. It would be repetitive, but it was alright! It meant that he could stockpile, prepare, and adapt to anything.

Still, his smile faded slightly as he remembered the warning about the upcoming Mech Siege. "Resources alone won’t win against machines. I’ll need firepower... strategy... maybe allies. I have three days of Beginner Protection to figure this out."
Kai closed the panel, then hesitated. "...Wait. If it’s really unlimited, I should test it now."
[ Gift Pack Selection ]
The message appeared as he used his Talent by using his mind.
Suddenly, he got the message.
[ Basic Gift Pack Selection ]
[ Energy Gift Pack ]
[ Entertainment Gift Pack ]
[ Food Gift Pack ]
[ Medical Gift Pack ]
[ Shelter Gift Pack ]
[ Stealth Gift Pack ]
[ Survival Tools Gift Pack ]
[ Transport Gift Pack ]
[ Water Gift Pack ]
[ Weapon Gift Pack ]

"Wait... It says here, Basic Gift Pack Selection... Will there be Intermediate or Advanced gift packs?" Kai muttered as he noticed how it was worded. This gave him a little hope that he might be getting something better.
After all, he just realized that the A.I. enemies might be using some androids or mech drones... Using a pistol or a hatchet against them might be a bit too difficult!
Nonetheless, he swiftly selected the weapon’s pack.
[ You have claimed a Weapons Gift Pack (Basic). ]
Just like that, he confirmed it in his Inventory.
[ Inventory:
Survival Tool Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Weapons Gift Pack (Basic) x1 ]
Kai gently nodded after seeing this.
"It worked... I actually got another pack."
He then crouched down and opened the Survival Tool Gift Pack first as he tapped it from his inventory.
He soon received a warning.
[ Do you want to open the Survival Tool Gift Pack? ]
Kai didn’t hesitate and tapped yes...
A faint glow appeared before it turned into solid objects. Just like that, all the contents appeared neatly before him.
The rope was coiled tightly... It seemed rough but sturdy. He unwound it slightly, testing the fibers with his fingers, and made a rough estimate.
"So it’s around ten meters... not bad," he muttered, satisfied that it was long enough for climbing or binding. This detail wasn’t included in the description after all.
Next, he checked the thermal blanket. He unfolded it carefully. It was larger than he expected, big enough to cover his entire body and even wrap around him twice if needed.
"This could keep me alive on freezing nights," he thought, folding it back into a compact square.
The fire starter was small but efficient. It was a magnesium rod with a striker. He tested the weight in his hand and imagined the sparks flying when scraped. It felt solid enough.
On the other hand, the compass was just as he had expected.
Then, he turned to the pocket knife, and it clicked open smoothly, its blade was sharp too...
Finally, the whistle... It was something he didn’t want to use, considering how it could attract survivors and enemies alike.
He then opened the Weapons Gift Pack.
He first checked the revolver...

"...Well," Kai’s lips curled into a helpless smile. He wanted it to be a standard handgun or something modern, maybe semi-automatic. But he could still accept it. He just needed to be careful of its recoil.
Kai then checked the cylinder. Six bullets were already loaded, just like the description said. Next to it was a small box of extra ammunition. He counted quickly.
"Twelve rounds... not bad."
The holster was plain leather, durable enough to strap to his belt.
He slid the revolver into it, adjusting until it rested tightly against his hip.
Lastly, the hatchet he got was small, but it was certainly heavy. He also confirmed that its edge was sharp enough to split wood or bone.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
He gave it a few test swings before hooking it into his belt. Then, he planned to return the other items to his inventory, but unfortunately, it wasn’t allowed.
[ Notice: Items obtained from Gift Packs cannot be returned to Inventory. ]
Kai rolled his eyes as he saw the picky system.
In any case, he glanced at his pants... He had six pockets in total.

He distributed the smaller items carefully... The compass and whistle in his left pocket, the fire starter and pocket knife in his right. The rope he looped and tied to his belt, while the folded blanket.
As for the folded thermal blanket, Kai decided not to carry it for now.

Instead, he placed it neatly on the ground to mark his "spawn point." The wind tugged at its edges, threatening to lift it away, so he crouched down and slid the blanket halfway under a mound of trash.
To be sure, he grabbed a broken chair leg nearby and pressed it firmly across the top, pinning the blanket in place.
"There," he muttered.
It wasn’t elegant, but at least the blanket wouldn’t fly off or vanish in the shifting garbage.
Now he had a clear marker to remind him where he had first arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Beginner Protection’s Limit
paragraphs: Kai held the spare ammunition, and thankfully, it fit neatly into another pocket. It was also secured tightly so it wouldn’t spill.
Once everything was in place, he felt ready.
"Alright. Organized."
Now that he knew that the items could not be returned to the Inventory, he made sure not to open Gift Packs unless necessary.
Still, Kai decided to open his Gift Pack Selection panel to store more of them in his Inventory.
[ Inventory:
Energy Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Entertainment Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Food Gift Pack (Basic) x5
Medical Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Shelter Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Stealth Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Survival Tools Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Transport Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Water Gift Pack (Basic) x5
Weapon Gift Pack (Basic) x1 ]
That took quite some time, since there was no bulk selection. He had to select the gift packs one by one.
Still, he decided to stock more Food and Water Gift Packs for obvious reasons.
Once satisfied, he tightened his grip on the hatchet and patted the revolver at his side.
With his gear secured, he rose to his feet and scanned the endless garbage dump. The stench was still overwhelming, but now he felt a little more prepared.
Whoosh!
A breeze brushed past him from the east, and Kai decided to follow it.
’Now, what do we have here... I hope this garbage dump has some hidden treasures or something.’Kai mused as he recalled Atom from a movie he watched before.
It wasn’t exactly like this garbage dump, and it was more like a scrapyard... However, he was still hopeful.
That treasure
"Maybe I should find an area filled with broken machines like that scrapyard,"Kai muttered as he continued to scan his surroundings while moving.

Well, the piles of spoiled food and decaying waste were also getting unbearable, so he had to move... It was not just for the smell, but for the risk of disease. If he stayed here too long, he might get sick before the real danger even arrived.
The silence pressed on as he walked past mountains of trash, broken furniture, and rusted metal.
After some time, he reached the edge of the dump. A new message appeared before him.
[ Warning: Moving further will remove your Beginner Protection. ]
Kai stopped in his tracks. He stared at the invisible boundary and the world beyond it hidden by piles of debris.
"...So this is the limit," he muttered.
He exhaled slowly and turned in another direction, continuing to follow the breeze.
After a few minutes, Kai’s eyes lit up.
Farther off, he noticed sections of the dump where twisted metal shone faintly under the gray sky. Indeed, it was the scrapyard he was searching for!
There were shattered appliances, rusted engines, and fragments of old devices scattered in mounds. It wasn’t pleasant, but at least it didn’t have that rotting smell.
Kai preferred this area, but the presence of stale water and what seemed like lurking insects meant he had to remain vigilant.
Nonetheless, compared to the other area with a rotting smell, this was simply better.
"Better to stick near the machines. Less chance of infection... and maybe I can salvage something useful."
As long as he was careful not to get scratched by these rusted metals, he should be fine.
And since he wasn’t hungry yet, Kai focused on checking the scrapyard, carefully noting the layout of the garbage dump.
As he looked around, he noticed some unstable trash mounds that looked ready to collapse at the slightest touch, so he decided to avoid them for now...
"Nothing..."
After a careful search, he left the scrapyard area. Well, he wanted to map the entire place covered by the Beginner Protection.
Whenever he received the warning that he was about to leave the Beginner’s Protection area, he would then stop and change direction.
Still, he made mental notes of salvage zones where there were piles of broken machines, twisted scrap metal, and shattered appliances that might prove useful later.
"Aahhh..."
Kai was a bit surprised after noticing some rats scurrying about.
Squeak-squeak!
They darted between piles of debris.
’So I have some neighbors here...’
Their beady eyes shone in the dim light before disappearing into cracks and tunnels beneath the trash.

Kai wrinkled his nose. Without his Infinite Gift Pack talent, he’d probably have been forced to filter or boil the stale water nearby, and maybe even cook rats for meals. The thought alone made him shudder.
He pressed onward, and he felt really thankful for the sturdy boots he had.
He didn’t need to worry about what he was walking on because of it. Whether it was rusted fragments, broken glass, or brittle plastic, his boots made him feel safe.
"Hmm?"
Kai paused at a mound of shattered appliances...
He crouched and brushed away dust and grime from a dented washing machine drum. He thought that he saw a snake, but it turned out to be wires that dangled loosely when he tried to lift it.
He continued mapping the area, mentally dividing it into zones.
There were general waste or food rot to the west, insects near stagnant water, unstable mounds scattered throughout, and metal scraps to the east.
It wasn’t much, but at least he had a clearer picture of his surroundings.
As he felt that he had completely mapped the area, the rats scattered suddenly, vanishing into the trash as if fleeing from something unseen.
"Hmm?"
Kai felt something was off as he tightened his grip on the hatchet.
Then he felt it... At first, it was barely noticeable, but the vibration grew stronger, sending a shiver up his boots.
’Something’s coming!’

[ Inventory:
Energy Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Entertainment Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Food Gift Pack (Basic) x5
Medical Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Shelter Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Stealth Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Survival Tools Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Transport Gift Pack (Basic) x1
Water Gift Pack (Basic) x5
Weapon Gift Pack (Basic) x1 ]
That took quite some time, since there was no bulk selection.
He had to select the gift packs one by one.
Still, he decided to stock more Food and Water Gift Packs for obvious reasons.
Once satisfied, he tightened his grip on the hatchet and patted the revolver at his side.
With his gear secured, he rose to his feet and scanned the endless garbage dump.
The stench was still overwhelming, but now he felt a little more prepared.
Whoosh!
A breeze brushed past him from the east, and Kai decided to follow it.
’Now, what do we have here...
I hope this garbage dump has some hidden treasures or something.’Kai mused as he recalled Atom from a movie he watched before.
It wasn’t exactly like this garbage dump, and it was more like a scrapyard...
However, he was still hopeful.
That treasure
"Maybe I should find an area filled with broken machines like that scrapyard,"Kai muttered as he continued to scan his surroundings while moving.
Well, the piles of spoiled food and decaying waste were also getting unbearable, so he had to move...
It was not just for the smell, but for the risk of disease.
If he stayed here too long, he might get sick before the real danger even arrived.
The silence pressed on as he walked past mountains of trash, broken furniture, and rusted metal.
After some time, he reached the edge of the dump.
A new message appeared before him.
[ Warning: Moving further will remove your Beginner Protection. ]
Kai stopped in his tracks.
He stared at the invisible boundary and the world beyond it hidden by piles of debris.
"...So this is the limit," he muttered.
He exhaled slowly and turned in another direction, continuing to follow the breeze.
After a few minutes, Kai’s eyes lit up.
Farther off, he noticed sections of the dump where twisted metal shone faintly under the gray sky.
Indeed, it was the scrapyard he was searching for!
There were shattered appliances, rusted engines, and fragments of old devices scattered in mounds.
It wasn’t pleasant, but at least it didn’t have that rotting smell.
Kai preferred this area, but the presence of stale water and what seemed like lurking insects meant he had to remain vigilant.
Nonetheless, compared to the other area with a rotting smell, this was simply better.
"Better to stick near the machines.
Less chance of infection... and maybe I can salvage something useful."
As long as he was careful not to get scratched by these rusted metals, he should be fine.
And since he wasn’t hungry yet, Kai focused on checking the scrapyard, carefully noting the layout of the garbage dump.
As he looked around, he noticed some unstable trash mounds that looked ready to collapse at the slightest touch, so he decided to avoid them for now...
"Nothing..."
After a careful search, he left the scrapyard area.
Well, he wanted to map the entire place covered by the Beginner Protection.
Whenever he received the warning that he was about to leave the Beginner’s Protection area, he would then stop and change direction.
Still, he made mental notes of salvage zones where there were piles of broken machines, twisted scrap metal, and shattered appliances that might prove useful later.
"Aahhh..."
Kai was a bit surprised after noticing some rats scurrying about.
Squeak-squeak!
They darted between piles of debris.
’So I have some neighbors here...’
Their beady eyes shone in the dim light before disappearing into cracks and tunnels beneath the trash.
Kai wrinkled his nose.
Without his Infinite Gift Pack talent, he’d probably have been forced to filter or boil the stale water nearby, and maybe even cook rats for meals.
The thought alone made him shudder.
He pressed onward, and he felt really thankful for the sturdy boots he had.
He didn’t need to worry about what he was walking on because of it.
Whether it was rusted fragments, broken glass, or brittle plastic, his boots made him feel safe.
"Hmm?"
Kai paused at a mound of shattered appliances...
He crouched and brushed away dust and grime from a dented washing machine drum.
He thought that he saw a snake, but it turned out to be wires that dangled loosely when he tried to lift it.
He continued mapping the area, mentally dividing it into zones.
There were general waste or food rot to the west, insects near stagnant water, unstable mounds scattered throughout, and metal scraps to the east.
It wasn’t much, but at least he had a clearer picture of his surroundings.
As he felt that he had completely mapped the area, the rats scattered suddenly, vanishing into the trash as if fleeing from something unseen.
"Hmm?"
Kai felt something was off as he tightened his grip on the hatchet.
Then he felt it...
At first, it was barely noticeable, but the vibration grew stronger, sending a shiver up his boots.
’Something’s coming!’

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Hidden Shelter
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes widened as the vibration intensified.
Crank!
A harsh scrape of metal against metal rang out, and a section of twisted scrap shifted.
He immediately turned toward the sound and saw it.
"Ahhh..." Kai’s breath caught. Something was being lifted.
A mound of junk, which had seemed immovable before, revealed its secret: a cleverly concealed hatch. Barbed wire slid aside as it creaked open just ten meters away.
Kai immediately dropped into a battle stance. He tightened his grip on the hatchet and drew his revolver.
Although he wasn’t an expert, he had at least practiced with airsoft guns. That experience mattered now, even if the stakes were real.
Still, he reminded himself: the main enemies couldn’t enter his Beginner Protection Area. Anyone appearing here was probably Neutral at the very least.
So I’m not alone after all...
The system had mentioned a starter region, but it had never said he would be the only one here. That realization sent a chill down his spine.
From the hatch, a man emerged slowly. His lower body remained in the steep stairwell beneath, while his upper half leaned into the open air.
Kai noticed the man’s unkempt hair and grime-covered skin immediately, but what stood out most was the strange eyepiece strapped over his left eye, like a watchmaker’s loupe.
The man’s gaze fixed on Kai. He seemed curious rather than hostile.
"So... another survivor ended up here?" the man said. "Where the heck are you guys coming from? Whatever. Since you’re human, come on... before the drones sweep the area. They have heat detectors!"
Kai hesitated with the revolver still in his hands. Yet the man didn’t flinch at his weapon. His tone carried concern, not threat.
Cautiously, Kai lowered the revolver slightly, keeping the hatchet ready in his other hand. He studied the stranger carefully as he stepped closer.
The man’s lower body remained hidden in the stairwell, and Kai could see just how steep it was inside.

"Don’t be scared," the man said. "This is one of the human shelters left after those damn A.I. took over. We need a hand here... If you can work, we can feed you. Nuts, mostly. Don’t expect too much."
Kai’s mind raced. Slowly, it clicked into place: this starter region wasn’t just a random location, it was a hidden shelter.
All of those who had selected this Apocalypse during the Selection might have been sent to scattered human shelters.
Kai took a deep breath and chose to follow the man for now...
"I’m Russel," the man said casually as they began descending the stairs.
Kai nodded, keeping the hatchet ready. He also noticed the knob that Russel turned to close the hatch.
The stairwell was narrow, steep, and made of scrap metal. It was roughly five meters deep. Each step creaked under their weight, but it held firm.
The lower they went, the colder and damper the air became. Still, the stench of rot from the garbage dump above had faded.
As they reached the bottom, Russel motioned for Kai to follow him along a steep pathway.
’Ohh... They have electricity.’

Kai’s eyes lit up as he noticed bulbs fixed along the corners of the tunnel. The walls were reinforced with steel beams, and though the floor was uneven, since it was littered with debris from years of repairs and expansions, it was still passable.
"This way," Russel muttered. "The real shelter is further down. We’ve been trying to make it... livable."
Kai followed silently. Most of the bulbs flickered or barely gave off light, forcing him to watch his footing, but he could make out more of the structure opening ahead.
As they walked, Russel started explaining, almost like he was talking to himself.

"Just so you know, this place isn’t just a hiding spot. It’s a proper shelter. Four people arrived here just a few minutes ago. I was told to check all the entrances, make sure no one got left behind... and that’s when I found you."
Kai gently nodded. "Other entrances?"

Russel chuckled. "Yeah. Of course... We needed many escape routes if needed. Hidden stairwells, trapdoors, concealed tunnels... they’re everywhere. Some even lead into the city, but that’s suicide. Anyway, as long as you’re not lazy, you can probably live for a long time."
That’s a lot of information, so Kai felt grateful.
"Thank you, Mr. Russel... This shelter, does it have a name?"
Russel nodded. "This place is calledHaven-45. Don’t ask why, just remember it. Everyone here calls it that."
Kai blinked. "Haven-45... okay. But... why build all this? Who’s running it?"
He asked cautiously. He didn’t have other intention aside from knowing more about this place.
However, Russel just shrugged, unconcerned.
"Doesn’t matter who. The past doesn’t matter. You don’t get points for being someone’s son, daughter, or whatever. If you survive, you survive. That’s enough. But..."
He glanced down at the pathway, then back at Kai... "This shelter isn’t just for waiting to die. We’re trying to get stronger..."
That caught Kai’s attention. With a Mech Siege coming, a shelter full of people willing to fight was exactly what he needed.
"How many people?" Kai asked.
Russel gave a grim smile. "Before you and the four new arrivals? Forty. Now... forty-five."
"Forty-five people... all underground?"

Russel nodded. "Yep. And every one of them’s got a reason to be here. Doesn’t matter who you were, what you did... once you’re inside, it’s about survival. If you can work, you eat. If you can’t... well, better hope you figure it out fast."

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Their Choices
paragraphs: Kai felt that the Haven-45 Shelter was far more organized than he had expected. This would definitely help when the siege came.

The two of them continued along the steep pathway. During this time, he noticed that along the narrow path, there were plenty of rusted pipes, dangling wires, and old support beams that crisscrossed overhead.
It gave the impression that the entire shelter had been built slowly, bit by bit, patched together from whatever could be salvaged.
Then, as Kai thought of asking him about the A.I. Rebellion, Russel spoke as if he could read his mind.
"By the way... I know you have lots of questions. I get it. You want to know everything. Who’s here, what’s going on, why the A.I. hasn’t wiped us out yet..." He shrugged.
"Don’t expect all the answers. But we’ll let you know what you should know... Then, learn as you go. That’s all I can tell you."
Kai nodded.
’Fair enough.’
Finally, the narrow pathway opened into a larger chamber.
The first thing that he noticed in this chamber was the box-like dividers that were probably rooms for the residents.
Then, he also noticed that flickering LED panels, patched-together generators, and crates of supplies that filled the central area...
A handful of figures moved quickly, checking equipment, stacking supplies, and tending to small fires.
Russel nodded toward them.
"Those are the four who arrived just before you. Don’t worry, they’ve already been briefed. You’ll meet them properly soon. For now... just get your bearings. This is your new world, kid."
Kai took a deep breath. The smell of metal, oil, and faint smoke filled his nostrils.
It wasn’t the best, but it was better than the situation outside.
The shelter felt cramped, but it was bearable.
Soon, Kai arrived at the gathering spot where four other people like him were...

"Alright... Stay here for now. I’ll just tell the manager to make your IDs. It’ll prove that you belong to Haven-45. It might be useful someday." Russel said before he left, leaving Kai with the other four, who seemed to be a little nervous or restless.
Unlike him, who had surrendered himself to this new reality, these four still looked worried and perhaps couldn’t accept what was happening.
Kai studied the four carefully.
They were all Caucasians, with one female among them. Each looked to be in their thirties, their faces tense and restless as if still struggling to accept this new reality.
Aside from that, all of them wore the same kind of Starter Gear that Kai had received.
It was the dark jackets, multi-pocket pants, sturdy boots, and belts with simple pouches.
There was no doubt that they were also sent here by the System.
Breaking the silence, Kai decided to start the conversation.
"It seems that we’re all dragged here... Did you all select the A.I. Rebellion willingly? I’m Kai, by the way."
The four exchanged uneasy glances before one of them finally spoke.
"Y-yes... I’m Wallace," the man said. At this point, his voice was still shaky, but he slowly calmed down as he continued.
"I got three options... Zombie Outbreak, Ragnarök, and A.I. Rebellion. I chose this."
Kai looked at him closely. Wallace had short blond hair, a square jaw, and a build that suggested he had worked with his hands before.

Wallace also studied Kai. His eyes lingered on Kai’s fair skin, dark hair, and sharp features. Kai’s appearance stood out among them, and Wallace seemed to note his calm attitude despite the situation.
Handsome, composed, and already carrying himself like someone prepared for survival.

However, Kai noticed something else. Despite their different backgrounds, they all understood each other perfectly. It seemed that the system had clearly removed any language barriers, ensuring communication was seamless.
Another man stepped forward next.
"I’m Ralph," he said before he turned to Wallace. To be honest, he hadn’t expected that there were other choices. He thought everyone had the same options.
Nonetheless, everyone noticed that his brown hair was thinning, and he wore glasses that were slightly cracked at the edges.
"Ahem... my options were Zombie Outbreak, Alien Invasion, Magic War, and A.I. Rebellion. I figured machines were more predictable than magic or aliens... so here I am."
He hadn’t even considered the Zombie Apocalypse.
The female survivor then spoke after him.
"I’m Claire," she said softly. Her auburn hair was tied back in a rough ponytail, and her eyes showed that she had just finished crying.

"It seems that there are a lot of Apocalypse choices I didn’t get. My options were Demon Invasion, Ragnarök, Divine Judgment, and A.I. Rebellion. I didn’t want to deal with gods or demons... so I picked this. At least machines can be fought with logic and weapons."
As they talked, the atmosphere was slowly being lifted. It seemed that a simple conversation was all they needed.
"Ohhh... everyone has unique options, huh."
Then, the last man introduced himself with a sigh.
"Name’s Victor," he muttered. He had a heavier build, with broad shoulders and a beard that made him look older than the rest.
"My options were Alien Invasion, Deep Sea Awakening, Parasitic Evolution, and A.I. Rebellion. I hate the ocean, and parasites... no thanks. So I went with this. Doesn’t mean I’m happy about it."
Kai nodded slowly, taking in their words. Each of them had faced different choices, yet all had ended up here, in Haven-45, under the same banner of survival against machines.
"Looks like we all chose the same battlefield," Kai said quietly.
"To be honest, I got a total of twelve choices."
Hearing this, everyone was shocked!
Previously, they had all been worrying about their spouses, children, parents, or even their pets that they had left behind. However, they were now curious about what other Apocalypses there were!

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Talents
paragraphs: For a moment, the chamber was filled with silence. The four stared at Kai, their earlier worry about families and pets momentarily replaced by curiosity.
"Twelve...?" Ralph muttered, adjusting his cracked glasses. "We only had a few... Why would the system give you so many?"

After learning the others’ choices, they realized that there were nine Apocalypses: Alien Invasion, A.I. Rebellion, Deep Sea Awakening, Demon Invasion, Divine Judgment, Magic War, Parasitic Evolution, Ragnarök, and Zombie Outbreak.
"What are those missing Apocalypses?" Wallace asked curiously. He couldn’t think of any other type of Apocalypse anymore.
Claire, on the other hand, had a different idea. "Does that mean... you’re different? Special? Or maybe... chosen?"
Kai shook his head firmly. "No. I don’t think it’s about being chosen."
Then, he listed the Apocalypses he had been given, and as expected, they all felt amazed. Apparently, there were still Dragon Awakening, Fairy Realm Collision, and Lycans versus Vampires.
"Ahhh! What a waste! I should’ve gotten that option. I want to be a Lycan..." Wallace suddenly said, surprising everyone.
"Fairy Realm? Is it related to something like goblins, orcs, elves, and dwarves? That’s..." Claire muttered, feeling that she would’ve chosen that instead.
As for Ralph and Victor, they simply felt curious why Kai had all the options available.
Nonetheless, Kai decided to shift the topic. "Do you remember the message we all saw when we selected this Apocalypse?"
The others paused as they tried to recall it. However, after some time, they still shook their heads.
Kai smiled helplessly, then repeated it slowly so they wouldn’t forget:
"The fate of the continent is in your hands. Survive and earn the title that is rightfully yours, and save your own world..."
"It seems that we have to earn a title to save our own world. Probably referring to Earth. Maybe... there’s still a chance to return."
Everyone’s eyes lit up.
"Ahh! That’s right!"
"I remember now..."
"I read something like that."
They had failed to notice it before, since they were too focused on their Gift Packs and the shock of arrival. Now, the words made sense.
Wallace clenched his fists. "So if we survive long enough... if we earn that specific title... we can go back?"
Kai nodded. "Well... that’s what it sounds like. Our families, our homes... they’re not gone yet. The system gave us a path. Let’s just survive here, fight here, and maybe we can return."
Although he didn’t have a family to return to, he still wanted to go back—since no machine would hunt him there.
With Kai’s encouragement, the atmosphere shifted. The despair that had hung over them like smoke began to clear. Finally, everyone had a clear goal.
"Destroy these goddamn machines," Victor muttered.
"If that’s the way back, then I’ll fight until I drop," Wallace added.
Claire managed a faint smile. "At least now we know what we’re fighting for."
Ralph exhaled slowly. "Then we need to learn everything about the A.I. from Russel and Augustine. If Haven‐45 is going to survive the Mech Siege, we need intel."

Claire added, "And we should talk about our Gift Packs and Talents too. The Gift Packs are just items, so we can share those openly. But Talents... those seem personal. Maybe we don’t need details, just a general idea of what each of us can do. That way, when the Beginner Protection ends, we’ll know who’s suited for combat, support, or survival."

Seeing no rejection, Claire decided to take the lead since she had suggested it. "Alright. I’ll start. My Talent is related to physical strength... but remember, I don’t have combat experience. I’m just a convenience store clerk. I can lift heavy objects, but if possible, don’t make me fight."
Ralph pushed his glasses up and spoke without hesitation...
"I’m good with guns. My Talent isSharpshooter’s Focus," he said directly.
"Unfortunately, I didn’t select the Weapon Gift Pack. I chose the Shelter Gift Pack instead... so I have a tent with me."
He gave a small shrug, half‐embarrassed. "I hope they have gun here or something."

Wallace chuckled before stepping in. "Mine’sIron Stamina. I don’t get tired easily, and it boosts my regeneration too. Cuts, bruises, exhaustion... I recover faster than most. It’s not that awesome, but I can definitely keep going when others drop from exhaustion."
Kai nodded thoughtfully. "That’s useful. Endurance and recovery are critical in this environment."
Victor sighed. He actually liked these Talents that they have. He would trade it to someone else if it were possible.

"My Talent’sMechanic. I have no experience, but the system says I can repair machines, weapons, and other devices as long as I study them for a bit. Well, it’s probably decent in some cases, but it’s only a Rare Talent."
The others, except Kai, looked at him curiously.

Victor realized that these guys had no idea, so he continued, "I played a lot of games when I was young. In those, Talents or Skills were graded. Common, Uncommon, Rare, and others like Epic, then higher tiers like Legendary, Mythic, and even Divine. Mine’s Rare. Not bad, but not the best either."
Ralph whistled softly. "Ohhh... Rare sounds pretty damn good... But I have Superior! Is it above Rare or below?"
"Ugh... I’m not sure." Victor replied. He felt that it was higher than Rare, but such matters depend on the developers.
Claire nodded. "I thought it’s not important... My Talent is just Uncommon..."
"That’s still amazing..."
"No one has a Common Talent then?"
"Even if you have, that’s alright!"
Kai studied them all carefully. Claire had strength talent, Ralph had accuracy talent, Wallace had stamina talent, and Victor was actually a mechanic!
All passive, but together they were a solid foundation.
He felt the system had deliberately scattered abilities to force cooperation.
Then, one by one, the four survivors turned their eyes toward Kai.
They had shared their Talents already and only Kai remained!

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Haven-45
paragraphs: Gulp...
Kai knew he had to reveal his Talent since they would eventually see it anyway. However, he wasn’t sure if this was the right idea.
His Talent was... strange. Too strange.
He still recalled that at first, the system had given him something not too insane:
[ Weekly Gift Cycle (Rare) ]

It was a Talent that guaranteed he’d be supplied with three Gift Packs of his choice every week. It was already decent, since there were ten Gift Packs to choose from, and he could select what he needed depending on the situation.
But then, an error had flashed across his vision. The system had glitched for some reason, and when it stabilized, his Talent had evolved, or perhaps completely changed!

[ Infinite Gift Pack (SSS): You can claim an unlimited number of Gift Packs at any time. There are no restrictions on frequency, quantity, or type. This talent grants continuous access to supplies, ensuring that Gift Packs are always available whenever you choose to obtain them. ]
Kai still didn’t understand why. And he didn’t plan to inform them about it, since that would only lead to endless questions.
Whatever the case, his Talent was now ranked SSS, far beyond anything the others had mentioned.
He considered for a moment before speaking. He couldn’t reveal everything... not yet.
"My Talent... it’s related to Gift Packs," Kai said slowly. "I can get more of them, but only if I fulfill certain conditions. Well, it’s not free."
The others straightened as they heard his Talent. It was unusual or strange, even.
"So there’s a Talent like that," Ralph muttered.
"I thought everything was related to the body..." Claire added.
"Me too... so weird talents related to the system itself are possible..." Victor said thoughtfully, though he had far more questions in his mind about this ability.
"That’s true... then there might be a Talent that gives free Level Ups or something," Wallace remarked with a laugh.
Certainly, since Kai’s talent was possible, there might be more absurd abilities out there.
Kai, on the other hand, just smiled faintly.

There was no need for payment or trade to get Gift Packs. However, he decided to condition them into believing he could only obtain Gift Packs if payment was involved. As for what that payment was, he didn’t know yet.
He would have to consider it later. Perhaps there was a currency in this Apocalypse, and he would simply claim that was the cost.

Indeed, Kai was already considering the possibilities of earning wealth with these Gift Packs. Since he could claim them endlessly, they could become the most valuable resource in Haven‐45. He could sell them, barter them, control their flow, or even run this whole shelter...
But he kept those thoughts to himself.
Just then, footsteps echoed down the chamber. Two figures appeared at the entrance.
Russel, the one who had found Kai and Claire earlier, entered. Beside him was Augustine, who had discovered Ralph, Wallace, and Victor at the garbage dump before bringing them here.
Russel smiled, seeing that the five recruits had already adjusted. They no longer looked worried or panicked.
"Good. You’re all looking great! Again... welcome to Haven‐45."

The two of them were here to inform Kai and the others about various matters. The first thing was the distribution of food, sleeping arrangements, the currency they used, and, of course, the work they would be expected to do for the shelter.
But before that, Augustine reached into a small pouch at his side. His hand emerged holding five simple wooden tokens, each carved into a rough oval shape.
The surface was smooth but they were unpolished. Still, they were etched with faint lines that resembled roots or veins.
He handed one to each of the recruits.
"Take these," Augustine said. "They represent Haven‐45. As long as you carry them, you belong here."
Kai turned the token over in his hand.
At first glance, it didn’t look special. It was just a piece of carved wood, lighter than it should be, with no markings that seemed important. But Augustine’s tone suggested otherwise.

"These tokens aren’t just symbols," Augustine continued. "They can’t be detected by any A.I. or machine. That’s why we use them. If you’re ever outside, or if you encounter another shelter, this proves you’re not an intruder. It shows you’re part of us."
The others examined theirs curiously.
Ralph squinted at the faint grooves, while Wallace rubbed the surface with his thumb.
"Mhmm... I don’t see anything special."
Claire held hers close as if it were a lifeline. "Let’s just keep it safe."
Victor nodded as he tucked it into his pocket immediately. He even tried to store it in his System Inventory, but it failed.
Of course, they all wanted to ask where the tokens came from or how they were made, but Augustine’s expression made it clear that no explanation would be given.
"They’re special," Augustine said simply, as if closing the matter. "That’s all you need to know."
Russel added, "Keep them safe. Lose it, and you’ll have a hard time proving you belong here."
Kai and everyone else nodded. They didn’t understand the origin, but they all understood its importance. In a world ruled by machines, anything undetectable was priceless.
With that said, Augustine straightened and gestured toward the chamber. "Now... let’s talk about how Haven‐45 operates."
Soon, it felt as if the five of them had entered a seminar.
They learned that even though the shelter only had forty people, its operation was seamless.
The survivors here were divided into Combat, Technical, Logistics, Sustenance, and Command roles
The Combat Division included Scouts like Russel, who ventured outside to track machine patrols. There were also Frontline Fighters and Marksmen who provided ranged support from elevated positions.

The Technical Division had Boiler Room Operators and Engineers who maintained power and ventilation. Mechanics repaired weapons and salvaged drones, while Electricians or Wire Technicians kept the shelter’s systems running.
The Logistics Division was composed of Quartermasters who managed supplies, builders and repair crews, and sanitation workers.

The Sustenance and Medical Division included Cooks and Food Handlers who prepared meals, Medics who treated injuries, and Foragers or Resource Gatherers who sometimes ventured out to scavenge food and materials.
But just as Augustine was about to continue, several steps echoed from behind.
Then, a deep but amused voice rang out...
"Ho~ What do we have here? Wait—a female recruit?! Finally!"
As the man spoke, his eyes locked on Claire, and he couldn’t help but lick his lips in excitement.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Scarcity
paragraphs: Both Russel and Augustine frowned upon seeing their arrival.
Their presence immediately shifted the atmosphere.
Even without their introduction, each of them seemed arrogant with their eyes sweeping over the new recruits like they were some sort of products.
Claire stiffened as all three of them looked at her with a familiar gaze.
It was a lecherous gaze that was unashamed, and it made her instinctively take a step back. Kai and everyone else noticed this.
Wallace and Ralph exchanged uneasy glances.
Although they were both Level 1, they would definitely fight if these three dared to do something inappropriate.
The two Scouts also noticed this, so they had to mediate. They didn’t like these men either, but they kept their composure.
Russel cleared his throat.
"Ahem... These are the operations leaders of Haven‐45. They oversee the divisions and keep the shelter running."
Augustine added, "They are the sons of the Elder, the one who originally managed this place. Age has forced him to step back, so authority was divided among them."
The three men stood proudly as their names were spoken. They looked at the two scouts, waiting for them to get introduced.
Realizing that they were not going to leave, Russel had no other choice but to introduce them properly.
"The first is Keagan," Russel said, gesturing to the broad-shouldered man with a scar across his cheek. His smirk was directed at Claire, and he seemed to be very pleased with something.
"He oversees combat operations."
"The second is Julian," Augustine continued, pointing to the lean man with messy black hair and bony features. His gaze also lingered on Claire with the same distasteful hunger.
"He manages logistics."
"And the third is Damon," Russel finished, nodding toward the tallest of the three, and of course, his grin was no less unsettling.
"He handles technical operations."
Kai studied them carefully. Keagan, Julian, and Damo...
They were definitely three scumbags who had inherited authority not through merit, but through blood.
Then, once again, Russel reminded them.
"They’re sons of the Elder, the oldest survivor in Haven‐45, whose wisdom had once guided the shelter."
Russel and Augustine didn’t badmouth them. Instead, they explained the importance of their roles, how each division was vital to survival, and how the three leaders coordinated operations.
Kai and the others also noticed that even if their words were professional, their eyes showed disdain.
The three command leaders finally decided not to linger any longer. Yet before they left, each of them stole another glance at Claire, their eyes lingering far too long.
Thud!
As soon as the chamber door closed behind them, Claire exhaled heavily... She suddenly felt weak.
She was already in her mid-thirties, and seeing those arrogant men in their twenties looking at her like that filled her with unease. The others noticed her discomfort, but no one spoke of it.
Russel broke the silence instead.
"You’ll have to get used to it. There aren’t many women here. Only eight, to be exact." His tone was matter-of-fact, but his frown showed he didn’t approve of how the leaders behaved.
He shifted the topic quickly. "Now, about compensation. Don’t expect wages or coins. There’s no money here. You work, you eat. That’s the deal."
Wallace raised a brow. "So... food is the payment?"

Russel nodded. "Food and water. But don’t imagine anything fancy. Most of what we have are nuts grown underground. They’re bitter, hard, and barely filling. The water comes from a deep well. It isn’t clean, not by old standards, but it doesn’t make us sick. Somehow, it keeps us alive."
Claire grimaced. "That’s... not much."
Russel’s expression hardened. "It’s survival. If you want more than that, you’ll have to earn it."
Victor tilted his head. "Earn it how?"
Russel hesitated, then sighed. "If you manage to scavenge something important outside, something the shelter needs, the three leaders can take it and exchange it for a drop of gold liquid."
Everyone looked at him in confusion.
Ralph adjusted his cracked glasses and asked, "Gold liquid?"
Russel wasn’t in the mood to explain, but he gave them the basics.

"It’s from before. From the government, or whoever was fighting the A.I. back then. They used it for gene enhancement. Strengthened the body, sharpened the mind, improved reflexes, and muscle control. A whole vial could somehow change a person. But here... you’ll only ever get drops. One drop reward for each major achievement. If you want to feel the effect, you’ll need a lot of contributions."
Kai nodded slowly, piecing it together.

So the three scumbags were managing the gold liquid. That explained why no one dared to cross them. It was their concept of leveling up. Their way of controlling power, and judging by Russel’s tone, they probably didn’t have much of it left.
Augustine gave a wry smile. "The machine that produces the gold liquid is probably in one of the larger shelters, not here. So if you ever get a drop, consume it immediately. Don’t risk losing it."
Wallace chuckled, trying to lighten the mood. "Well, are we not getting one for free as a gift or something?"
Russel’s sharp look silenced him. "No. Nothing here is free. Remember that."

The chamber fell quiet again. The recruits exchanged uneasy glances. Food was scarce, water was barely clean, and the only path to strength was through drops of a mysterious liquid controlled by corrupt leaders...
Then, their eyes lit up as they looked at Kai!

Everyone looked at him in confusion.
Ralph adjusted his cracked glasses and asked, "Gold liquid?"
Russel wasn’t in the mood to explain, but he gave them the basics.
"It’s from before.
From the government, or whoever was fighting the A.I. back then.
They used it for gene enhancement.
Strengthened the body, sharpened the mind, improved reflexes, and muscle control.
A whole vial could somehow change a person.
But here... you’ll only ever get drops.
One drop reward for each major achievement.
If you want to feel the effect, you’ll need a lot of contributions."
Kai nodded slowly, piecing it together.
So the three scumbags were managing the gold liquid.
That explained why no one dared to cross them.
It was their concept of leveling up.
Their way of controlling power, and judging by Russel’s tone, they probably didn’t have much of it left.
Augustine gave a wry smile.
"The machine that produces the gold liquid is probably in one of the larger shelters, not here.
So if you ever get a drop, consume it immediately.
Don’t risk losing it."
Wallace chuckled, trying to lighten the mood.
"Well, are we not getting one for free as a gift or something?"
Russel’s sharp look silenced him.
"No.
Nothing here is free.
Remember that."
The chamber fell quiet again.
The recruits exchanged uneasy glances.
Food was scarce, water was barely clean, and the only path to strength was through drops of a mysterious liquid controlled by corrupt leaders...
Then, their eyes lit up as they looked at Kai!

chapters.title: Chapter 11: The Condition
paragraphs: Claire and Wallace had chosen the Weapon Gift Pack, wanting something they could use to fight the machines. They believe that the revolver would surely help, even with its limited bullets.

Ralph, on the other hand, had selected the Shelter Gift Pack, believing that good sleep and recovery from fatigue would be just as important as weapons. It didn’t just include a tent, but also a sleeping bag that assured him that he’d get some comfort in this harsh world.

Victor had gone with the Stealth Gift Pack. In his mind, hiding was always better than fighting. With its camouflage suit, smoke grenade, and other tools, he felt his chances of survival would be higher if he avoided direct confrontation.
However, none of it was important in front of Kai... His unusual Talent allowed him to obtain Gift Packs endlessly... though at a price.
Now, the four had the same thoughts, perhaps they could purchase Food Gift Packs or other essentials through him... Unfortunately, they knew it would be difficult since they had nothing to offer yet.
At the very least, they had no idea what Kai needed.
Russel noticed their silent exchange but chose not to comment. Instead, he continued his briefing.
"Since you’re here now, you should understand what we’re up against. Out there, the machines are everywhere, but in this region, only two types come around regularly."
The five turned to him, listening closely.

"The first are the Swarmers," Russel explained. "They’re foot-sized drones. They attack in clusters. Well, they’re certainly weak alone, but quite terrifying in numbers. They’re used for scouting, surveillance, and harassment. We don’t mess with them. Destroying one only calls more, and before you know it, you’ll be buried under a storm of them."
Claire shivered at the thought. The others nodded grimly, none of them eager to provoke such a swarm.
"Alright... those drones are a no-go," Wallace muttered.
Seeing that they understood, he continued.
"The second are the Sentinels. They’re humanoid patrol units as tall as you..." Russel said while pointing at the tallest in the group, Wallace.

"They’re the standard soldiers of the A.I. army. They’re armed with rifles, and if you’re unlucky, plasma cutters. They don’t report back to their base unless they’re low on energy, so if you have the strength, you can destroy them without drawing more attention. They’re dangerous, but manageable."
Victor nodded slowly. "So we can fight them. Very well."

Russel wryly smiled at that comment. "If you can. Eliminating a Sentinel is worth it. Their loot is valuable. They have energy cores, weapon fragments, and sometimes even servo parts or mechanical devices for robotics... Those drops keep the shelter running. Power, repairs, upgrades... everything depends on scavenging from them."
Wallace’s eyes widened. "Sounds like they’re walking treasure chests."
Augustine shook his head. "You wouldn’t say that if you knew how strong they are. Anyway, don’t get greedy. Hunt too many, and you’ll draw something worse, the Breakers."
The recruits waited for Russel to elaborate.
He didn’t want to discuss this, but since Augustine had already mentioned it, he might as well introduce it.

"They’re heavy, spider-like machines that were built for sieges. They smash barricades, bombard shelters, and tear through defenses like paper. I’ve only seen one in more than ten years here. Trust me, you don’t want to see another. As long as you’re not greedy, you only need to worry about the drones above and the Sentinels on the ground."
Kai and the others finally understood just how fragile their situation was. Swarmers in the skies, Sentinels on the ground, and the possible threat of Breakers if they pushed too far.
They kept this information in mind.

Finally, Russel gave a short nod. "That’s all you need to know for now. Get some rest, learn the routines, and prepare yourselves. We’re still deciding where to put you all to work. We’ll discuss it and let you know later."
"Do we not have a say in this?" Wallace asked. He actually wanted to work where he could properly use his Iron Stamina Talent.
However, Russel just waved his hand dismissively. "Mhmm? Of course not. At least not on your first day. Just go with the flow for now."
Augustine added, "We’ll check on you later. For now, stay sharp."
With that, the two men left, pointing out where the recruits could rest. Apparently, there were empty corners and makeshift "rooms" patched together from scrap metal.
Kai and the others didn’t need to ask more questions. They already had a gist of the situation. The shelter was organized, but its leadership was rotten at the core.
For now, they had nothing to do but settle into their quarters that looked so terrible.
Thankfully, Ralph had a tent he could use for some privacy, along with a sleeping bag. However, the others weren’t lucky.
"Ugh... How am I going to rest here?" Wallace muttered while looking at his corner. They do not have beds, chairs, or tables at all.
It really was just a corner with a divider made of scrap metal!
Claire also felt uncomfortable as she wanted to use the toilet. Furthermore, she still felt grimy after slipping in the garbage dump earlier.
She wasn’t smelly, but the filth clung to her skin. She wanted to take a bath, but she knew that she didn’t have the luxury to do it.
After all, even the three leaders a while ago didn’t seem to have taken a bath for weeks!
Victor also examined the empty space they had been given.
’It’s not even a proper living quarter, just an open area sectioned off like cubicles.’
With a sigh, all of them turned to Kai, their eyes filled with expectation.
They hoped he would finally reveal the conditions they had to meet in order to obtain a Gift Pack.
