Ralph, with his Sharpshooter’s Focus Talent, knew that he just had to have a clear view of the target, so he liked this idea and nodded.
"Got it.
If the old man tries anything, he won’t even get the chance."
Wallace and Victor also agreed with this plan.
Kai smiled.
He was probably overthinking this matter, but since they were about to meet someone who had possibly consumed more Gene Enhancement Serums than them, he had to be cautious.
"With this setup, even if the Elder has bad intentions, we can fight back or retreat.
The risk is still there, but it should give us some assurance."
The group agreed.
Still, Kai didn’t push them to move immediately.
They had just survived the Sentinel attack, and exhaustion weighed on everyone.
"Rest first," Kai ordered.
"We’ll go when we’re ready."
Soon, the kitchen crew was already preparing water, and after a few moments, steaming cups of tea were placed before them.
The tea, a simple but comforting blend, was from the Food Gift Packs.
For a brief moment, the group sat together in silence, sipping slowly, letting the warmth settle in their bodies.
Only after this pause did Kai rise to his feet.
"Alright.
Let’s go."
With Russel and Augustine’s men stationed at the chamber entrance, hatchets in hand, and the five leaders in formation, they finally descended into the lowest part of Haven‐45.
The air grew colder as they moved deeper...
Soon, the sound of the medical devices became faintly audible even before they reached the Elder’s room.
At last, they stood before the Elder’s door.
Russel and a few others already waited there.
"The Elder is inside.
He’s waiting for you all."
Kai glanced at his companions, then stepped forward.
"Let’s see what this old man has to say."
The door creaked open, and the warm air of the chamber swept out.
On the bed lay the Elder, who seemed frail and motionless.
There were only tubes and wires keeping his body alive.
For a moment, he seemed barely conscious.
However, his eyes snapped open, and they were glowing with a strange light.
Gene Skill!
The group froze as the Elder’s gaze locked onto them!

chapters.title: Chapter 29: Explosion!
paragraphs: For a moment, it seemed as if the frail old man was about to unleash something devastating. The glow in his eyes seemed sinister, as if a laser was about to hit them...
But then... nothing happened as the glow in his eyes disappeared.
The Elder remained motionless, his body was still bound by tubes and wires, and his eyes were the only part of him showing signs of power.
The group froze, caught between fear and confusion, as they had no idea what had happened just now.
Then, they heard the Elder’s raspy voice, startling them all.
"...You are not ordinary. You’re not from here, are you?"
Kai stiffened with his revolver still half‐raised while Claire squinted her eyes as she guessed the Elder’s Gene Skill just now.
However, Victor, who was just at the door, spoke.
"What the hell does he mean? What do you know?"
Wallace and Victor exchanged uneasy glances but just remained silent.
’The old man guessed it right...’
The Elder’s eyes lingered on them before he spoke again. "Humans... yes. But your bodies are different. It seemed altered as if you carry something that does not belong to this world."
Kai was now curious.
They had only arrived on this continent a few days ago, after being forced to choose which apocalypse to enter.
Out of all the options, the five of them had landed in this A.I. Rebellion Apocalypse. No one here should have known that truth. Yet this frail old man had seen it without them saying a word.
Kai lowered his weapon slightly and asked. "What did you do just now? Is that the ability you got after consuming that gold liquid?"
The Elder closed his eyes briefly, then opened them again.
"My ability... I call it Sage Eyes. They appraise, and they detect some things others can’t perceive."
Hearing that they were not harmed or cursed just now, the tension eased, but only slightly.
"So you scanned us..." Claire muttered.
Kai pressed on. "Then why call us here?"

The Elder’s lips trembled as he spoke, "Because my time is ending. I will not live much longer. Before I go, I wanted to meet the ones who changed Haven‐45. I do not blame you for eliminating my sons. They were blind, selfish. But you... you must become strong. Strong enough to defeat them..."
Ralph frowned. He wasn’t sure what this old man wanted, but he was hoping that he wouldn’t be wasting their time.
"It’s good to hear that you’re not blaming us... I can assure you that we’ll kill the A.I. Army... or whatever they are."
The Elder stared at Ralph for a moment before he spoke again. "The A.I. Civilization."
Kai and the others froze. "A.I. Civilization?" he repeated, disbelief in his tone.

The Elder nodded weakly. "You think Aria, the greatest A.I. created by humans, rebelled on its own? No. Something else pushed it. An external force... a Mechanical Civilization that does not come from this world."
Everyone paused as they heard this.
First of all, they didn’t even know about Aria, the one who rebelled against humanity... Now, they also learned that aside from Aria, there was a third party involved.
"Another civilization? You mean... machines from outside?" Victor

"Yes," the Elder whispered. "Not born of this world. Not born of humanity. They came from beyond, and they touched Aria and twisted her. What you see now, the Sentinels, the endless Swarmers, the rebellion... is not just her will. It is theirs."
Kai finally understood the backstory of this world.
’So that’s why this apocalypse feels different... why the machines evolve so fast. It isn’t just rebellion. It felt more like an invasion.’
Claire also appreciated this information and nodded. "Then... defeating this A.I. Aria isn’t enough, huh..."
The Elder blinked in agreement.
"Defeating Aria is only the beginning. If you survive... if you grow... you may be the only ones who can stand against them."
Silence fell again, broken only by the hum of the medical devices. The group exchanged uneasy glances.
It seemed that defeating this Apocalypse would not be so easy...
Kai finally spoke, his tone calm but heavy. "Why tell us this?"
The Elder’s lips curled into a crooked, evil smile, one that didn’t match the frailty of his body.
Seeing this, the group felt a chill run down their spine...
"Because... I need to buy some time." The Elder said.
Kai’s Keen Sense was triggered instantly. His instincts screamed that something was wrong. The faint hum of the medical devices shifted, and there was an irregularity, almost like a hidden signal.
It’s a trap!
Without hesitation, Kai raised his revolver and fired. The shot rang through the chamber, striking the Elder’s shoulder.
Although he was close, his aim was terrible!
Still, he knew that there was no time, so he shouted!
"Run!"
The group didn’t hesitate. Claire grabbed Kai’s arm and pulled him back, while everyone else also retreated...
Boom!
The Elder’s bed suddenly erupted in a violent explosion with flames and shrapnel tearing through the chamber.
The blast shook the walls, sending dust and debris raining down...
They were able to run out of the chamber, but the shockwave hurled them against the wall!
"Ugh..." Russel and Augustine’s men, who were previously at the door and slower to move, were also barely holding their ground as the blast caught them.
Even Kai hit the floor hard with his ears ringing...
"That old man..." Kai wanted to curse, but he clutched his head in pain.
They were tricked!

chapters.title: Chapter 30: The Warning
paragraphs: Claire had actually shielded Kai with her body. Her Physical Strength Talent allowed her to absorb the brunt of the shock, and she seemed perfectly fine.
In the meantime, Ralph coughed violently as he inhaled dust and smoke.
"Damn it! The old man wanted revenge in the end." Wallace cursed, dragging Victor toward the corridor.
For several minutes, the corridor was filled with coughing, groans, and the sound of debris settling.
Dust hung thick in the air, choking their lungs and stinging their eyes.
Kai forced himself upright, his ears still ringing.
His body ached from the blast, but his Level 5 stats gave him resilience.

The pain dulled quickly as his muscles stabilized faster than any ordinary survivor could manage. He then noticed that Claire was already on her feet, brushing dust from her arms, her Talent certainly made her recovery just as swift.
Ralph, Wallace, and Victor also seemed shaken but alive. Their quick retreat saved them from the worst of the blast.
’Good...’
Kai heaved a sigh of relief after realizing that they were all doing fine.
He then scanned the corridor with his Keen Sense, sweeping for signs of danger.
"Everyone alright?" he asked.
Russel staggered forward while coughing into his sleeve. Augustine also leaned against the wall, his face pale.
"We’re... we’re fine," Russel managed. "Barely."
Kai nodded and asked, "Where did he get those explosives? That bed wasn’t just rigged... it was packed. Enough to collapse his whole chamber."
Russel shook his head, frustration etched across his face. "I don’t know. None of us knew. The Elder was bedridden, surrounded by carers. We never saw anything like that brought in."
Augustine added, "We checked supplies. Nothing was missing. If he had explosives, I think his sons had previously set it up there."
Kai clenched his jaw...
He exhaled sharply, forcing down his anger. "Fine. Let’s inspect this place further. There might be other hidden explosives we’re not aware of."
Just then, Kai finally turned to the notification he just received.
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +550 Experience Points ]

Kai gently nodded after seeing this notification... It just showed that the Elder must have a very high level compared to him. That would explain why he got so many Experience Points despite his minimal participation.
He dismissed the window and looked at Russel.
"What do you think? Since the elder is gone. What about his followers?"

Russel stepped forward. "Some still followed him, even if he was bedridden. It’s all because they’re grateful that they were given shelter... But since he’s gone now, I’m sure they’ll just adapt to the current leader."
Kai nodded. In any case, he planned to earn their trust through his Infinite Gift Pack Talent, so he knew what to do.
With the Elder gone, Haven‐45 had no choice but to look to Kai and his companions for leadership.
The survivors were shaken, but Kai’s calm authority and the group’s decisive actions earned them respect. No one dared to challenge their rule.
Kai quickly made a decision after meeting everyone...
No scavenging outside!
The Sentinels were still prowling, and the shelter had suffered enough losses. Instead, he would rely on his Infinite Gift Pack Talent to sustain everyone.
Within hours, Haven‐45 began to change.
Kai summoned Food Gift Packs one by one, distributing canned goods, instant noodles, granola bars, and tea bags to be stored in the warehouse.
With his leadership, no one would be hungry. The survivors even laughed when mayonnaise became a staple condiment, spreading it on their granola bars and mixing it with noodles.
From the Water Gift Packs, Kai provided filled bottles, filters, and purification tablets. The collapsible buckets were set up in the kitchen area, ensuring clean water was always available.
The Shelter Gift Packs transformed sleeping arrangements. Survivors who had been huddled on cold floors now had sleeping bags, thermal blankets, and ponchos.
Flashlights lit up the darker corners of the underground halls, making the shelter feel less like a tomb and more like a home.

It didn’t end there, Kai distributed the Entertainment Gift Packs and brought unexpected joy. Playing cards became a nightly ritual, harmonicas echoed faint tunes in the corridors, and journals gave survivors a way to record their fears and hopes.

As for the Medical Gift Packs, they were a godsend to the medical practitioners. First aid kits, antibiotics, and painkillers were stocked in a central infirmary. After many years, Haven‐45 had a reliable supply of medicine. Dustin, who had cared for the Elder, now oversaw the medical corner, grateful for the resources.

Then, Kai handed out Stealth Gift Packs, and soon every survivor had camouflage suits. They weren’t just clothing... They were durable, practical, and uniform. The shelter looked more organized, and its people started resembling a disciplined group rather than scattered refugees.
From the Survival Tools Gift Packs, ropes, knives, and fire starters were distributed. These tools gave survivors confidence, even if they never stepped outside.
As for Transport Gift Packs. Folding bicycles weren’t usable yet, but the helmets that were included were needed.
On the other hand, the Weapon Gift Pack’s revolvers weren’t distributed for obvious reasons.
Then, on the third day, Kai inspected the underground field with others...
Rows of peanuts grew in the dim light, tended by survivors who had once relied on the Elder’s sons for supplies.
"This is surprisingly well organized."
Kai checked the soil, the irrigation pipes, and the growth...
It was actually quite stable. It was no wonder they could rely on peanuts and various leaves to survive.
Kai was quite satisfied with this and decided to increase the personnel taking care of this field.
Then, as they were getting used to life inside the shelter, the System finally reminded them of the upcoming Mech Siege!

chapters.title: Chapter 31: The Upcoming Mech Siege
paragraphs: The glow of the System interface appeared before Kai and the other survivors.
[ Global Event is Here! ]
[ Upcoming Hostile Operation: Mech Siege ]
[ Countdown: 48 Hours Remaining ]
[ Objective: Defend designated shelter against mechanical assault for 72 hours. ]
[ Failure Condition: Shelter destroyed. All survivors eliminated. ]
[ Rewards: Experience Points, Loot Drops, Survivor’s Medal, Potential Title Upgrade, and others ]
’Right... thanks for reminding me,’Kai mused as he studied the message.
He was about to dismiss the window when another notification immediately followed.
[ Additional Notice: Enemy forces calibrated to shelter population and average level. ]
[ Estimated Enemy Composition: Sentinel Units, Swarmer Drones, and Beastframe‐class Units. ]
After getting all this information, Kai wasted no time.

He gathered everyone in the central hall to discuss the matter. Survivors stopped what they were doing. Some were still clutching camouflage suits, others holding bowls of noodles, as they stared at him while he relayed the information.
After all, only the five survivors from Earth had received the System’s message. The rest of the shelter’s residents had no idea what had just happened.

Then, after Kai explained what would occur in two days, the expected reaction came... They were all filled with worry. Most of them had never fought against the living machines, but they knew how terrifying they were.
Claire also felt nervous as she spoke. "We have two more days. I hope we don’t get too many of them attacking us."
Ralph cursed. "Should we try to excavate that rifle buried in the collapsed northern tunnel?"
Victor gave a helpless smile. He knew that whatever had been buried there was most likely destroyed already. Instead, he focused on the message from the system.
"It says here that the difficulty scales with population... then the more people we protect, the harder the siege will be. This will be tough..."

Kai nodded grimly. "Which means we can’t afford mistakes. At the very least, this is just the first Mech Siege. Since everyone’s only beginning this apocalypse, they probably won’t make it too hard... or no one would survive."
"That’s true..." Claire agreed. It wouldn’t make sense if the siege were impossible to defeat.
Kai then asked the division leaders about their preparations.
After feeling satisfied, he turned to Russel and Augustine. "Double the guards at every entrance. No one leaves, no one enters without our say."
Russel straightened. "Understood."
Augustine added, "I’ll start stockpiling weapons. Everyone capable of fighting will have their guns soon."
Kai had no choice but to trust them. He wasn’t sure how many enemies would besiege them, and he needed every ounce of help.

Then he looked at Victor. "Your Mechanic Talent is about to become critical. Every device, every tool... repair it, reinforce it. Radios, solar chargers, water pumps, especially that massive door at the east tunnel entrance. If you can, help reinforce all the tunnel doors. Fighting Sentinels and other machines outside is suicide. We’ll have to destroy them in the narrow tunnels instead."
Victor’s eyes widened, but he nodded firmly. "I’ll get started right away."
Finally, Kai addressed everyone. "We have two days to prepare for three days of mechanical assault. We’ll use every resource we have and survive this. Trust me!"
The crowd erupted in cheers.
"Yes! We trust Leader Kai!"
"We will defend this shelter!"
"Let’s all work together!"
Kai glanced at the notification that had appeared at the bottom left of his vision.
[ Event Progress Tracker Activated ]
[ Time Remaining: 47 Hours, 52 Minutes ]
’We can do this...’Kai thought, clenching his fist.
The survivors moved quickly under Kai’s orders. Hatchets were distributed, additional camouflage suits provided, and the corridors echoed with hammering and repairs.
As for the revolvers, Kai planned to distribute them before the siege.
On the other hand, Victor threw himself into his work. His Mechanic Talent gave them a crucial advantage.

Radios were rewired, their static signals cleared. Solar chargers were adjusted to store power more efficiently. Water pumps in the peanut field were reinforced to prevent leaks. Folding bicycles were tightened and stored, ready for emergency escape.
Even beds and medical tools were cleaned and repaired, ensuring that if there were wounded during the siege, they would have a place to recover.
Each repair gave Victor 1 to 5 experience points. It wasn’t much, but it added up, so he was quite happy doing a lot of work.

Meanwhile, Kai summoned Gift Packs as much as he could. Food and supplies were stockpiled in the warehouse, medical kits filled the infirmary, and survival tools were distributed to every member of the shelter.
In just a single day, the shelter began to look less like a crumbling refuge and more like a fortified base.
At night, survivors still gathered in the hall, playing cards or listening to harmonica tunes. It was their way to stay sane in this underground shelter.
Though the fear of the siege was still present, Kai’s leadership gave them hope.
[ Time Remaining: 24 Hours, 14 Minutes ]
’One more day...’ Kai thought, silently praying that there wouldn’t be casualties on their side during the siege. It might be difficult to achieve, but he clung to hope.
Meanwhile, while Kai and the others rested, Claire slipped out of her sleeping bag and left her tent in the sleeping area.
She moved quietly through the corridors until she reached the vacant chamber once used by resource gatherers to store scavenged materials.
It was empty now since no one had gone out to gather in days.
Claire checked the shadows carefully, confirming she was alone. Then she whispered softly...
"Come out...

"It says here that the difficulty scales with population... then the more people we protect, the harder the siege will be.
This will be tough..."
Kai nodded grimly.
"Which means we can’t afford mistakes.
At the very least, this is just the first Mech Siege.
Since everyone’s only beginning this apocalypse, they probably won’t make it too hard... or no one would survive."
"That’s true..." Claire agreed.
It wouldn’t make sense if the siege were impossible to defeat.
Kai then asked the division leaders about their preparations.
After feeling satisfied, he turned to Russel and Augustine.
"Double the guards at every entrance.
No one leaves, no one enters without our say."
Russel straightened.
"Understood."
Augustine added, "I’ll start stockpiling weapons.
Everyone capable of fighting will have their guns soon."
Kai had no choice but to trust them.
He wasn’t sure how many enemies would besiege them, and he needed every ounce of help.
Then he looked at Victor.
"Your Mechanic Talent is about to become critical.
Every device, every tool... repair it, reinforce it.
Radios, solar chargers, water pumps, especially that massive door at the east tunnel entrance.
If you can, help reinforce all the tunnel doors.
Fighting Sentinels and other machines outside is suicide.
We’ll have to destroy them in the narrow tunnels instead."
Victor’s eyes widened, but he nodded firmly.
"I’ll get started right away."
Finally, Kai addressed everyone.
"We have two days to prepare for three days of mechanical assault.
We’ll use every resource we have and survive this.
Trust me!"
The crowd erupted in cheers.
"Yes!
We trust Leader Kai!"
"We will defend this shelter!"
"Let’s all work together!"
Kai glanced at the notification that had appeared at the bottom left of his vision.
[ Event Progress Tracker Activated ]
[ Time Remaining: 47 Hours, 52 Minutes ]
’We can do this...’Kai thought, clenching his fist.
The survivors moved quickly under Kai’s orders.
Hatchets were distributed, additional camouflage suits provided, and the corridors echoed with hammering and repairs.
As for the revolvers, Kai planned to distribute them before the siege.
On the other hand, Victor threw himself into his work.
His Mechanic Talent gave them a crucial advantage.
Radios were rewired, their static signals cleared.
Solar chargers were adjusted to store power more efficiently.
Water pumps in the peanut field were reinforced to prevent leaks.
Folding bicycles were tightened and stored, ready for emergency escape.
Even beds and medical tools were cleaned and repaired, ensuring that if there were wounded during the siege, they would have a place to recover.
Each repair gave Victor 1 to 5 experience points.
It wasn’t much, but it added up, so he was quite happy doing a lot of work.
Meanwhile, Kai summoned Gift Packs as much as he could.
Food and supplies were stockpiled in the warehouse, medical kits filled the infirmary, and survival tools were distributed to every member of the shelter.
In just a single day, the shelter began to look less like a crumbling refuge and more like a fortified base.
At night, survivors still gathered in the hall, playing cards or listening to harmonica tunes.
It was their way to stay sane in this underground shelter.
Though the fear of the siege was still present, Kai’s leadership gave them hope.
[ Time Remaining: 24 Hours, 14 Minutes ]
’One more day...’ Kai thought, silently praying that there wouldn’t be casualties on their side during the siege.
It might be difficult to achieve, but he clung to hope.
Meanwhile, while Kai and the others rested, Claire slipped out of her sleeping bag and left her tent in the sleeping area.
She moved quietly through the corridors until she reached the vacant chamber once used by resource gatherers to store scavenged materials.
It was empty now since no one had gone out to gather in days.
Claire checked the shadows carefully, confirming she was alone.
Then she whispered softly...
"Come out...

chapters.title: Chapter 32: Claire’s Secret
paragraphs: Claire stood alone in the vacant chamber, waiting for an answer.
However, there was no response. Still, she didn’t mind it as she knew that the spirit she was calling had an attitude.
She whispered again, and this time, it sounded firm...
"Come out..."
Finally, the air shifted. A shadow moved at the edge of the chamber. It was faint and formless, yet undeniably present.
Claire’s heart pounded.
She had felt this presence since the day she awakened her Talent, but she had never dared to speak to it directly when there were others around.
[ Talent: Fifth Sin (Epic): Power grows as wealth is accumulated. Wealth includes food, tools, weapons, valuables, and resources. A Spirit companion bound to the user. ]
When everyone was discussing their Talents before, she had lied. She had repeated the words whispered by the shadow at her side, Physical Strengthening Talent...Uncommon Rank...
At first, she didn’t really want to lie, but the spirit companion sounded so scary. It was like a devil whispering in her ears, and she wanted it to shut up.
Still, that wasn’t a complete lie since her power or physical strength would indeed improve as long as she gathered wealth...
"You finally called for me."

Claire flinched, her fists tightening as she listened to the voice. "I... I had no choice. The siege is coming. I need to know what you are... what I really am. I need to know how to get stronger faster."
"You already know how to get stronger... Accumulate wealth."The spirit said.
Claire narrowed her eyes at the shadow or the spirit.
"No... I don’t think it’s just about piling up food and weapons. There has to be more to this Talent than simply hoarding things."
She was able to guess this much since there wouldn’t be a need for a spirit companion if that was all she could do.
The spirit chuckled after seeing Claire’s face...
"You are perceptive. Indeed, wealth is only the foundation. There are deeper layers to the Fifth Sin... powers you have yet to touch."
Claire’s heart pounded. "Then tell me."
The shadow then moved closer...

"If you desire, I can possess your body for a brief duration. In that state, your strength will surge beyond mortal limits. Sentinels will crumble before your fists, Swarmers will scatter like insects, and if you want to conquer this shelter, you can also do so with my help."
Claire froze. "Possession...? What’s the cost?"
The spirit’s tone changed, almost amused by the question once again. At this point, the spirit already understood Claire’s way of thinking.

"Payment is always required. You’re right... Each time I take control, a small portion of your permanent health will be consumed. Not stamina, not temporary health, but your true life force. Once gone, it cannot be recovered."
Her stomach twisted as she heard this. That was too much!
Permanent stats... that was something she couldn’t afford to lose recklessly.
The spirit then pressed on."But understand this... once possessed, you will be unstoppable. No machine will stand against you."
Claire clenched her fists, torn between temptation and caution. The thought of tearing through Sentinels with ease was intoxicating, but the price was too steep.
"...I see," she whispered finally.

"I really want to try it but since it’s that expensive, I hope that I won’t have a chance to use this ability. I can’t risk losing my health points. If I do, I’ll only shorten my future. But..." She exhaled slowly, feeling relieved that she had a trump card.
"At least now I know. If things get desperate, I have this possession..."
The spirit’s laughter echoed faintly before fading back into silence.
"Wise choice. Keep me as your hidden blade. When the time comes, you will know whether the price is worth paying."

Soon, Claire just stood alone in the chamber, trembling but strangely relieved. She had uncovered another layer of her Talent. It was dangerous, costly, but it could save her life and the people she wanted to protect.
Just like that, she turned back toward the sleeping area to continue resting...
The next morning arrived, and no one spoke much. They were all filled with anticipation. Every survivor knew what was coming.

Kai stood at the center of the hall, overseeing the final preparations. Revolvers were distributed one by one, each survivor receiving a weapon and extra ammunition. The clinking of bullets being loaded echoed through the corridors.
Even those who had never fired a gun before were given basic instructions. "Aim for the chest," Ralph muttered as he demonstrated, "and don’t waste bullets."

Kai then reviewed the defenses. Haven‐45 had seven remaining entrances in total. Four of them were wide tunnels, large enough for Sentinels and Hounds to march through. Those would be the main battlegrounds.
The other three were narrow paths, too small for the machines to fit. Guards were stationed there anyway, just in case, but Kai knew the real fight would be at the larger gates.

In the meantime, Victor was still busy, tightening bolts on the eastern tunnel’s massive door. His Mechanic Talent had been invaluable, reinforcing weak points and ensuring the doors could withstand the first wave.
By midday, everything was ready. Food and water were secured, medical kits were stocked, weapons were distributed, and guards were posted.
As the timer ticked down, the survivors gathered in the central hall and waited silently.
Soon, the glow of the System interface appeared before Kai and the other Earth survivors.
[ Warning! ]
[ Hostile Operation Initiating: Mech Siege ]
[ Objective: Defend designated shelter for 72 hours. ]
[ Enemy Forces Approaching. Estimated Arrival: 5 Minutes. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 33: The A.I. Army’s Evil Plan
paragraphs: Kai stared at the glowing System interface as he felt strangely calm.
Finally, the wait was over...

The countdown had ended, and they had done everything they could during the past couple of days. Haven‐45 was fortified, the survivors were armed, and his group had also prepared multiple plans in case defending the shelter failed.
But then, he noticed some sort of changes in the system’s panel. It was quite similar to what had happened when he had been forcefully sent to A.I. Rebellion!
’Shit...’ Kai cursed as he didn’t like where this was going...
[ Unexpected state detected... ]
[ Additional Notice: Due to the unique situation of this area, the attacking mechanical army will arrive at a higher tier. ]
[ Warning: Enemy strength increased. ]
[ Secondary Objective Added: Captured humans detected within mechanical forces. You may choose to save or ignore the lives of the captured humans. ]
[ Note: Decision will affect the final rewards. ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "What...?"
The other four Earth survivors received the same message. Claire, Ralph, Wallace, and Victor exchanged confused glances. None of them had expected this.
"Captured humans?" Ralph muttered with disbelief. "What the hell does that mean?"
Victor frowned, his hands tightening around his tool belt. "Are they saying the machines are dragging people with them? Why?"
Claire’s face paled as she imagined the scenario. "If they’re alive... then the machines are using them."
The group fell silent, unsettled by the implications.
Five minutes passed.
Soon, the scouts stationed near the surface, armed with angled telescopes or periscopes, scanned the garbage field above. The wasteland that concealed their underground shelter felt different today.
Suddenly, one of them shouted, his voice trembling.
"Leader Kai! You need to see this!"
Kai rushed forward, climbing the observation ladder. He pressed the periscope to his eye, and what he saw made his blood run cold.
The Sentinels were advancing across the garbage field, their metallic bodies were still the familiar ones he had seen before.
But strapped to their bodies, tied crudely with wires and chains, were humans. Naked, bruised, and bound, their faces twisted in agony, showing that they were still alive.
Each Sentinel carried two or three captives, their bodies lashed to the machines like grotesque shields.
"What the..."
The humans struggled weakly with their cries muffled by the distance, but their suffering was undeniable.
Kai lowered the periscope as he didn’t expect to make such a decision like this.
"They’re using people... as shields."
The scouts looked horrified. "They’re alive... but they’re being dragged like animals!"
Claire’s fists trembled.
"This... this is evil. These machines aren’t just rebelling. They’re torturing humans."
Wallace cursed under his breath.
"How do we fight them now? If we shoot, we’ll hit the captives!"
Victor’s voice trembled. "The System wasn’t lying. We really have to choose... save them, or ignore them."

The survivors gathered in silence, the weight of the decision pressing down on them. The mechanical army was approaching, stronger than expected, and now the battlefield was tainted with human lives bound to steel.
Kai clenched his revolver... Then, his Keen Sense also allowed him to sense at least 15 humans tied to six Advancing Sentinels.
’So this is their cruelty... this is what we’re up against.’
The Mech Siege had begun, and it was already far worse than anyone had imagined.
It didn’t take long before everyone learned about this...
The hall was filled with murmurs as they realized that these Sentinels were different.
The residents of Haven‐45, already pale with dread, now looked at Kai with pleading eyes.
"Leader Kai..." one of the older men spoke, his voice shaking. "We can’t save them. If we try, we’ll all die. Isn’t it better to ignore them? A necessary sacrifice..."
Others nodded reluctantly. "We barely have enough strength to defend ourselves. If we risk saving those people, the machines will tear through us."
"They’re already as good as dead," another whispered bitterly. "Better them than all of us."
The words stung, but Kai understood their fear. He glanced at Claire, Ralph, Wallace, and Victor. None of them spoke, but the weight of the decision pressed heavily on their shoulders.

Kai exhaled and nodded. "Listen to me. We don’t have the strength to save them now. Our priority is Haven‐45. If we manage to rescue anyone, that’s good. But if not..." His eyes hardened. "We won’t take the blame. Survival comes first."
The residents fell silent, some ashamed, others relieved. It was a cruel truth, but Kai’s calm authority steadied them.
Above, the Sentinels continued their march, dragging their captives like some kind of medals hanging on their bodies. But the scouts’ voices broke through again, this time with panic.
"Hounds!"

Kai rushed back to the periscope. Three mechanical beasts prowled the garbage field, their frames low to the ground, waiting. Their glowing eyes scanned the terrain and it wouldn’t be long before they could discover the entrance...
As expected, it didn’t take long before the alarm rang.
"The east entrance!" a guard shouted. "One of the Hounds found an opening!"
The ground trembled as the mechanical beast made its move. Its claws immediately tear into the reinforced door of the eastern tunnel.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
Sparks flew as metal screeched against metal.
Kai raised his revolver and ordered everyone.
"Positions! Everyone, get ready! The siege has begun!"
The survivors scrambled, gripping their weapons as they moved to the eastern tunnel.
The Sentinels were advancing above, the captives swaying helplessly on their frames, while the Hounds had finally struck below.
The Mech Siege was no longer a distant threat... It was here.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Survivors
paragraphs: ’What’s this?! Why am I still alive?’She opened her eyes and saw the ground swaying beneath her.
For a moment, she thought she was falling. Then the pain in her shoulders reminded her that she was still being hanged, upside down, tied cruelly to the chest of a marching Sentinel.
Her name was Sera, though the machines didn’t care.
To them, she was nothing more than a living shield, a body strapped to steel.
Her long, ash‐blonde hair dangled toward the dirt, streaked with grime and dried blood. Every step of the machine jolted her, giving pain through her spine and ribs.
It was horrible...
She no longer struggled. She no longer screamed. Her cracked lips parted only to whisper to herself. They were words no one could hear.
’Just let it end... let me die without pain.’
Sera had once been a medic in the old world, tending to the wounded in a refugee camp after the collapse.

She had saved lives with nothing but scraps of cloth and stubborn will. But when the Mechanical Civilization swept through, her camp was destroyed. She had tried to protect the children, tried to shield them with her own body.
However, the Sentinels had cut them down anyway. She was taken, bound, and dragged across the wasteland like a trophy.
Now, upside down, she felt her humanity slipping away. Her pale eyes stared at the garbage field below, dull and lifeless.
She remembered the faces of those she couldn’t save, and the guilt gnawed at her more than the chains.
Yet somewhere deep inside, a faint ember remained.
She thought of the promise she had made to a dying child in her arms..."I’ll keep fighting. I’ll keep you safe."
She had failed then. And now, she wanted nothing more than release. But fate had other plans...

Not too far from Sera, Althea was also bound cruelly with chains across the Sentinel’s torso. The machine carried her like a grotesque ornament. Her bare skin was already bruised and scraped from the rough bindings.

Her long, dark hair was already stiff from dirt, but that didn’t matter. Every step of the Sentinel would make her feel pain, and she couldn’t even pass out even if she wanted to because of the drug that was forcefully fed to her.
Her eyes, half‐closed, stared at the garbage field below.
At this point, she no longer struggled like many other captives. She had stopped fighting hours ago.
’I don’t want to be saved anymore...’she thought bitterly.
Similar to Sera’s wish, she also wanted to end this after suffering too much pain.

She had once been a teacher before the world collapsed. She had taught literature to children in a small provincial school. Before, her voice was always gentle, and her smile was always warm. She had loved books, stories, and the idea that even in a broken world, words could give hope.

But when the Mechanical Civilization rose, her school was destroyed. She fled with her younger brother, Miguel, wandering from one ruined settlement to another. They had survived together, sharing scraps of food, hiding from patrols, clinging to the faint hope of finding a safe haven.

That hope ended when the Sentinels found them. Miguel had been killed instantly, cut down by a machine’s blade. Althea had been captured, tied to steel, and dragged across the wasteland as a living shield.
Now, chained on a Sentinel, she felt her humanity slipping away. Her lips were cracked, her voice gone from screaming. Her once bright eyes were dull, reflecting only despair.
The Sentinel carried her forward, indifferent to her suffering.
She was nothing more than a tool, a barrier of flesh to protect its mechanical body.
Yet even in her despair, a faint ember lingered.
She remembered Miguel’s last words before the machines took him...
"Don’t give up, Althea, Someone will save us."
She wanted to believe it. But as the garbage field stretched endlessly beneath her, she whispered silently to herself, as she already lost her hope.
"Please... if anyone saves me... let it be quick. Let it be merciful."
Her fate seemed sealed, but suddenly, the Sentinel carrying her halted...
Althea’s half‐closed eyes opened.
The machine’s head turned, its glowing optics started scanning the horizon as if it had detected something. Of course, the chains binding her rattled against its steel frame as it turned its body.
Urgh...
She felt her stomach twist, and it was quite painful.
’What now...?’
The other Sentinels slowed as well, and their captives swayed in unison.
Even the Hounds prowling nearby froze. Soon, their claws were digging into the garbage field.
Althea’s heart thudded weakly. She didn’t know why, but for the first time since her capture, the machines seemed... cautious.
Then, through the haze of despair, she heard it.
There was a faint vibration beneath the earth.
It was subtle at first, like a distant rumble, but growing stronger with each passing second.
Her cracked lips parted as she whispered in disbelief, "What... is that?"
The Sentinel’s optics scanned once again while her grip on her chains tightened.
"W-what’s..."
The captives groaned as the machines shifted awkwardly, as if they were bracing for an impact.
Althea’s dull eyes widened just slightly.
Somewhere beneath the garbage field, something was moving.
And then...
Boom!
A deafening explosion erupted across the garbage field, shaking the ground beneath the Sentinels.

sentences.text: ’What’s this?!
Why am I still alive?’She opened her eyes and saw the ground swaying beneath her.
For a moment, she thought she was falling.
Then the pain in her shoulders reminded her that she was still being hanged, upside down, tied cruelly to the chest of a marching Sentinel.
Her name was Sera, though the machines didn’t care.
To them, she was nothing more than a living shield, a body strapped to steel.
Her long, ash‐blonde hair dangled toward the dirt, streaked with grime and dried blood.
Every step of the machine jolted her, giving pain through her spine and ribs.
It was horrible...
She no longer struggled.
She no longer screamed.
Her cracked lips parted only to whisper to herself.
They were words no one could hear.
’Just let it end... let me die without pain.’
Sera had once been a medic in the old world, tending to the wounded in a refugee camp after the collapse.
She had saved lives with nothing but scraps of cloth and stubborn will.
But when the Mechanical Civilization swept through, her camp was destroyed.
She had tried to protect the children, tried to shield them with her own body.
However, the Sentinels had cut them down anyway.
She was taken, bound, and dragged across the wasteland like a trophy.
Now, upside down, she felt her humanity slipping away.
Her pale eyes stared at the garbage field below, dull and lifeless.
She remembered the faces of those she couldn’t save, and the guilt gnawed at her more than the chains.
Yet somewhere deep inside, a faint ember remained.
She thought of the promise she had made to a dying child in her arms..."I’ll keep fighting.
I’ll keep you safe."
She had failed then.
And now, she wanted nothing more than release.
But fate had other plans...
Not too far from Sera, Althea was also bound cruelly with chains across the Sentinel’s torso.
The machine carried her like a grotesque ornament.
Her bare skin was already bruised and scraped from the rough bindings.
Her long, dark hair was already stiff from dirt, but that didn’t matter.
Every step of the Sentinel would make her feel pain, and she couldn’t even pass out even if she wanted to because of the drug that was forcefully fed to her.
Her eyes, half‐closed, stared at the garbage field below.
At this point, she no longer struggled like many other captives.
She had stopped fighting hours ago.
’I don’t want to be saved anymore...’she thought bitterly.
Similar to Sera’s wish, she also wanted to end this after suffering too much pain.
She had once been a teacher before the world collapsed.
She had taught literature to children in a small provincial school.
Before, her voice was always gentle, and her smile was always warm.
She had loved books, stories, and the idea that even in a broken world, words could give hope.
But when the Mechanical Civilization rose, her school was destroyed.
She fled with her younger brother, Miguel, wandering from one ruined settlement to another.
They had survived together, sharing scraps of food, hiding from patrols, clinging to the faint hope of finding a safe haven.
That hope ended when the Sentinels found them.
Miguel had been killed instantly, cut down by a machine’s blade.
Althea had been captured, tied to steel, and dragged across the wasteland as a living shield.
Now, chained on a Sentinel, she felt her humanity slipping away.
Her lips were cracked, her voice gone from screaming.
Her once bright eyes were dull, reflecting only despair.
The Sentinel carried her forward, indifferent to her suffering.
She was nothing more than a tool, a barrier of flesh to protect its mechanical body.
Yet even in her despair, a faint ember lingered.
She remembered Miguel’s last words before the machines took him...
"Don’t give up, Althea, Someone will save us."
She wanted to believe it.
But as the garbage field stretched endlessly beneath her, she whispered silently to herself, as she already lost her hope.
"Please... if anyone saves me... let it be quick.
Let it be merciful."
Her fate seemed sealed, but suddenly, the Sentinel carrying her halted...
Althea’s half‐closed eyes opened.
The machine’s head turned, its glowing optics started scanning the horizon as if it had detected something.
Of course, the chains binding her rattled against its steel frame as it turned its body.
Urgh...
She felt her stomach twist, and it was quite painful.
’What now...?’
The other Sentinels slowed as well, and their captives swayed in unison.
Even the Hounds prowling nearby froze.
Soon, their claws were digging into the garbage field.
Althea’s heart thudded weakly.
She didn’t know why, but for the first time since her capture, the machines seemed... cautious.
Then, through the haze of despair, she heard it.
There was a faint vibration beneath the earth.
It was subtle at first, like a distant rumble, but growing stronger with each passing second.
Her cracked lips parted as she whispered in disbelief, "What... is that?"
The Sentinel’s optics scanned once again while her grip on her chains tightened.
"W-what’s..."
The captives groaned as the machines shifted awkwardly, as if they were bracing for an impact.
Althea’s dull eyes widened just slightly.
Somewhere beneath the garbage field, something was moving.
And then...
Boom!
A deafening explosion erupted across the garbage field, shaking the ground beneath the Sentinels.

chapters.title: Chapter 36: Against the Sentinels
paragraphs: The heavy steps of the Sentinels shook the garbage field. At the same time, the chains rattled as the captives strapped to their mechanical bodies swayed helplessly.
Clank... Clank...
The Hound prowled ahead with its claws scraping against the ground as it scanned for enemies.
Kai didn’t hesitate when he saw what was happening. He raised his hand, not for another collapse, but for something different.
"Smoke!" he commanded.

Immediately, survivors pulled the small canisters from the Stealth Gift Pack. Pins were yanked, and thick plumes of gray smoke erupted across the battlefield. The haze spread quickly, swallowing the Sentinels and the Hound in a choking fog.
"Good..."
Soon, their optics started overworking as they struggled to adjust. For a moment, the machines halted, scanning wildly with their vision disrupted.
The survivors then disappeared into the haze, with their silhouettes slowly vanishing. Thanks to their camouflage suits from the same pack, they blended even further into the fog.
Kai also crouched with his revolver ready.
"Stay hidden. Let them reach the trap."
Just like that, the Sentinels advanced blindly. The Hound seemed to have better detection ability as it moved forward, with the Sentinels following behind.

’I guess highly advanced sensors weren’t a priority for the Sentinels,’Kai mused. Since they were mass‐produced, it wasn’t surprising that most of their parts were lacking. It was already impressive that they were all equipped with energy rifles.
Nonetheless, the second part of the plan was soon initiated.

Over the past two days, the survivors had prepared not just the shelter but also the battlefield. Using the fire starter from the Survival Tools Gift Pack, they had arranged piles of flammable debris like plastic scraps, oil‐soaked rags, and broken wood.
Now, as the machines stumbled into one of those spots, a survivor hurled a flaming torch.
Whoosh!
The fire caught instantly, creating a wall of flame. The Sentinels staggered and their captives shrieked as heat touched their bodies.
The Hound, the first to enter the trap, tried to leap back with its claws scraping against the burning ground. But the blaze spread fast, wrapping around its mechanical frame.
Suddenly, the battlefield was filled with smoke and fire.
Kai then reminded the group. "Hold position! Let the fire do the work!"
The machines thrashed with their optics glowing through the haze.

One Sentinel tried to raise its rifle, but flames engulfed its arm, melting plastic and warping metal. After some time, its legs began sinking into softened ground, trapped as the fire consumed the debris beneath it.

The other two Sentinels at the back managed to escape. Still, they tumbled onto their backs, crushing the unlucky captives strapped to them. Yet in the chaos, some chains and wires loosened, freeing other captives.
Kai couldn’t see this through the wall of fire, but he knew their advance had been stopped.
The Hound, however, was strong. It forced its way out of the flames, its armor scorched but intact.
Victor turned toward two members of the Resource Gatherer Team.
"Now!"
They carried the crude but powerful devices he had built himself, large taser‐like weapons improvised from scavenged parts, powered by batteries and a power bank from the Energy Gift Pack.
The Hound charged forward, intent on tearing them apart, but the two survivors didn’t care! Their devices were already sparking with raw electricity.
Thud! Thud!
The tasers slammed into the Hound’s mechanical frame.
Bzzzt!
Electricity surged, frying circuits and crawling across its body. The machine convulsed violently, its claws twitching.
"Hahaha! Is it really working? That looks good, man..." Wallace said as he saw this happen.
"Awesome! Victor, you have to make more of those!" Claire said excitedly.
The others were ready to shoot with their revolvers raised. They were prepared to fire if the tasers failed. But they didn’t.

"If I have the materials, I can make more," Victor said, proud that his Mechanic Talent had proven useful in the siege. Of course, this wouldn’t have been possible without Kai’s batteries and power bank, but still, Victor had shown his worth.
Just like that, only the three Sentinels remained.
Clank... Clank...
One of the Sentinels, still stuck, tried to move but failed to escape the pit of fire. Its rifle was gone, melted in the blaze, but its massive arms swung wildly.

Half of its body managed to push forward as it tried to break free. The two Resource Gatherers rushed in again with their taser‐like weapons. They slammed the devices into the Sentinel’s head, electricity surging up its frame.
Bazzz!
The machine convulsed with sparks bursting from its joints.
But this time, the devices couldn’t handle the strain.
Pop!
The tasers overloaded, and smoke started pouring out from their casings.
"Aahhh!"
The survivors dropped them, afraid of being electrocuted, but the damage was already done.
"I guess I have to make some changes..." Victor muttered after seeing that the weapon was only usable a couple of times.
Nonetheless, the other two Sentinels, still at the edge of the blaze, were soon able to stand up, and they tried to move forward.
They then started scanning for targets, but the haze distorted their vision. One lifted its massive leg, stepping into the burning debris.
Crunch...
The ground beneath it gave way, softened by fire and melted plastic. The Sentinel missed its footing, and its balance was messed up!
With a heavy crash, it toppled sideways into the flames.
The second Sentinel also attempted to adjust, but its sensors were sluggish.
It stepped forward, only to sink knee‐deep into the molten garbage.
Just like that, the blaze wrapped around its frame, consuming its armor.
Kai watched from cover in disbelief.
"They’re dumber than I thought..." he muttered.

chapters.title: Chapter 37: New Skills
paragraphs: The inferno raged until the Sentinels could no longer withstand it.
Their mechanical frames warped, their cores overheated, and soon they collapsed into the flames.
Just like that, the machines no longer moved!
Then, in the midst of the smoke, Kai and the five survivors glanced at the glowing notifications that appeared before their eyes.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +300 Experience Points ]
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Hound (E) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +100 Experience Points ]
Several more similar notifications appeared since six Sentinels and three Hounds had been defeated. The points were shared among the five, and although lower than before, they didn’t mind it at all.
Furthermore, every survivor had finally reached Level 5!
"I got it! My physique also improved!" Victor said. "Feels like I can work twice as fast now."
Claire blinked as she checked her own notification. "I’m level 5 as well! Wait... I’m still E plus."
"The requirement might be higher now, Claire... Still, everyone will finally get their Gene Skill!" Wallace replied.
"Yeah! Look!" Ralph said excitedly. The Gene Skill was what he was really excited about.
Kai just smiled as he also got the same experience points but he didn’t level up.
’Reaching Level 6 is tough...’He mused.
The four Survivors, on the other hand, immediately focused on their own notifications. They basically had the same notifications after Kai reached this level a few days ago.
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 5 ]
[ Health Points +50 ]
[ Spirit Points +10 ]
[ Gene Skill Points +1 ]
[ Physique Rating Improved: E+ ]
[ Inventory Slots Expanded: +1 ]
It was unfortunate that Claire remained E+ in her Physique Rating, but she could understand that it had a higher requirement now to advance.
Then, her eyes widened as she focused on the Gene Skill she obtained.
[ New Passive Gene Skill Activated! ]
[ Skill: Titan Grip (Level 0) ]
[ Description: Enhances raw physical strength. Increases lifting capacity, melee impact, and resistance against disarm attempts. ]
[ Note: Passive skills cannot be deactivated. Leveling requires Gene Skill Points. ]
She clenched her fists, feeling the subtle surge of power in her muscles. "I... I feel stronger already," she whispered.
Ralph also checked what he got.
[ Skill: Quickdraw (Level 0) ]
[ Description: Enhances weapon handling speed. Reduces reload time, improves weapon switching, and steadies aim while moving. ]
"It’s also a passive skill. Nice... This is perfect." Ralph commented. Of course, he immediately tried it as he aimed an object with his revolver. He could immediately tell the difference.
"Mine’s better." Wallace said as he also got his Passive Skill.
[ Skill: Swift Stride (Level 0) ]
[ Description: Enhances movement speed and agility. Reduces delay between actions and improves efficiency when retreating or advancing under pressure. ]
He actually got a movement buff! With his Stamina-Related Talent, it made him even better!
Finally, Victor also checked his own passive gene skill.
[ Skill: Adaptive Tinkering (Level 0) ]
[ Description: Improves improvisation with mechanical devices. Speeds up repairs, increases efficiency when modifying weapons, and grants instinctive awareness of mechanical weak points. ]
Victor’s eyes lit up as he stared at the notification.
"This... this is incredible." He crouched beside a discarded energy rifle. Soon, his fingers brushed the warped metal.

"This skill is awesome, Kai... I’m telling you. I can already see where it failed... and how to fix it. It’s like the machine is talking to me." His grin was wide, proud. "Give me time, and I’ll turn their weapons against them."
"That’s what I like to hear." Kai replied as he also wanted all the rifles fixed.
For now, however, he had produced buckets of water to finally put out the fire... It took a dozen buckets, but it didn’t take that long.
"Wait..."
As the smoke cleared, Kai’s keen eyes caught sight of three bodies near the burning spot. The chains had loosened during the chaos, dropping them to the ground.
Because of that, their forms were battered and barely recognizable through the dust and grime.
"Russel, Augustine!" Kai shouted.
The two men moved immediately. Both were seasoned in rescue, and soon, they rushed forward, pulling the bodies away from the heat.
Russel knelt beside them, ready to perform the first aid.
He checked pulses, and one of them just drew his last breath. Seeing his face and body condition, Russel believed that it might be better if he didn’t survive.
"One’s gone," he said quietly. "But the other two... they were still alive."
Russel was actually worried if they could treat those two women who had somewhat survived.
Their bodies were covered in bruises and scars. Their skin blistered from the fire, but faint breaths escaped their lips.
However, they were going to die at this rate. So they needed quick medical treatment.
"They’re breathing," Augustine confirmed, his voice firm. "We can still try saving them."
Without hesitation, they lifted the two patients and carried them toward the underground shelter.
"You’re in safe hands now... Don’t give up." Russel whispered.
Kai nodded at their quick response, but for now, he had to focus on the items they could loot from the defeated enemy units!

chapters.title: Chapter 38: Please, Work!
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes swept the field.

He knew the victory was temporary. According to the system, the mech siege lasted seventy‐two hours or three days, and this was only the first batch. More mechanical soldiers would arrive soon, so they had to move quickly.
"Resource team," Kai called out. "Start the salvage. We need every part we can get."
The Resource Gathering Team hesitated for a moment.
The process would be grim since there were human remains everywhere... Furthermore, none of them had much experience dismantling machines of this scale. These machines are too advanced for them.
They might also make mistakes and destroy important parts of them. However, realizing that Kai and the others would also assist, they immediately felt more confident.
"We... we’re on it, Leader Kai!"
"Let’s go!"

The team moved as they looked at the three Sentinels and two Hounds that were trapped in the collapsed part of the east tunnel. It was painted red since the blood and fleshly remains of human captives were still present.
However, the smell of the garbage field was stronger... At this point, they already had a strong stomach that could endure such stench, except for one.
"Ugh..." Claire turned away almost immediately. Her fists clenched as she couldn’t bear to watch any longer. The sight of broken bodies tangled in chains and wires was too much.
"I’ll... I’ll help with the traps," she muttered, leaving the salvage to the others.
Kai understood. He didn’t stop her, since he knew that not everyone could stomach this part of survival. Furthermore, creating more pit traps or flammable traps was also important.
Just like that, Russel and Augustine also endured the morbid scene as they helped sever the cables and chains that were tied around the Sentinels, previously used to trap their human captives.
For some time, they all worked together dismantling the Sentinels since they were just too heavy.
Dragging them back would also be tough, so they had to at least remove some of their parts. Then, they could easily transfer them to the warehouse, where they could be further studied.
Of course, there was one of them who would be very useful on this task.

Victor crouched beside a fallen Sentinel, his Adaptive Tinkering skill was already guiding his eyes. He pointed to a section near the chest cavity. "We can cut through here. This should be the Cognitive Processor Unit. It should be intact if the core didn’t overheat. We’ll need to cut through the armor."
Well, they had all received the system notifications about the high-value salvageable items within the Sentinels and Hounds.
[ Sentinel’s Salvageable Loot: Cognitive Processor Unit, Targeting Optic Lens, Exo‐Frame Armor Shard, Energy Power Cell, Plasma Rifle ]
[ Hound’s Salvageable Loot: Beastframe Neural Core, Beast Claw Component, Synthetic Muscle Fiber, Hydraulic Joint Cylinder ]
[ Note: Only high‐value salvageable components are listed. Common debris and low‐grade materials are excluded. ]
Just like that, the salvage began in earnest.
Wallace grunted as he lifted the hand of the Sentinel... "I’ll hold it steady. You work and cut it off properly."
After a few minutes, the Sentinel finally turned to a size they could safely and easily carry back to the shelter...
"Hurry. We don’t know how long before the next wave." Ralph reminded.
As soon as several parts were brought back to the storeroom of the shelter, Victor also returned and immediately got to work.
He used his various tools from the Repair Kit to pry open the chest plating. It was not easy, but soon, the dull glow of the Cognitive Processor Unit appeared.
"Got it," he said while carefully detaching the component.
Then, he got a notification from the system!
[ Item Obtained: Cognitive Processor Unit ]
[ Description: Central processor recovered from Sentinel core that stores combat data and tactical routines. ]
"Ohh... It’s really important... But, where am I supposed to use these things?" Victor muttered.
In the meantime, the others were still working on the remaining Sentinels and Hounds.
But after almost 15 more minutes, they finally brought back all the Sentinels and Hounds except for the ones burnt in the fire pit. It was still hot, and no one wanted to touch them.
Nonetheless, they immediately worked on a thorough dismantling process.
While there were still no enemies above ground, Kai immediately worked on another Sentinel with his knife, digging into the head unit.
Soon, he pulled free a cracked but usable Targeting Optic Lens.
[ Item Obtained: Targeting Optic Lens ]
[ Description: Precision lens recovered from Sentinel head unit. ]

"Whoa... I got a notification for this thing. I guess it’s really valuable, huh." Kai muttered after seeing a special notification for the lens. After all, the synthetic muscles and various parts of the Sentinels didn’t give him any notifications.
It seemed that the previous note from the system was real. Those were indeed high-value loots.
Russel and Wallace also managed to pry loose what they believed was the Exo‐Frame Armor Shard...
[ Item Obtained: Exo‐Frame Armor Shard ]
[ Description: Armored plating from Sentinel exo‐frames. ]
Just like that, the group continued taking all the ’high-value’ items and gathered them all together.
[ Beast Claw Component: Hardened claw fragment from Hound unit. ]
[ Synthetic Muscle Fiber: Artificial muscle strands recovered from Hound unit. ]
[ Hydraulic Joint Cylinder: Hydraulic joint removed from Hound limb. ]
For now, they were still unsure how to use them. They were even hoping that the system would teach them how to convert these things to usable goods.
Still, one of them was something they really wanted to use as quickly as possible.
[ Item Obtained: Plasma Rifle ]
[ Description: Standard‐issue rifle recovered from Sentinel unit. ]

"Victor... I’m begging you! Please make this thing work! We’re going to be attacked by those things for three days!" Wallace begged as he looked at Victor, frowning at the high-tech rifle on the table.
Kai chuckled as he tapped Wallace’s shoulder...
"Just trust him--" He was about to say more when Russel came rushing in.
"Leader Kai, both girls have regained consciousness," He reported.

sentences.text: Kai’s eyes swept the field.
He knew the victory was temporary.
According to the system, the mech siege lasted seventy‐two hours or three days, and this was only the first batch.
More mechanical soldiers would arrive soon, so they had to move quickly.
"Resource team," Kai called out.
"Start the salvage.
We need every part we can get."
The Resource Gathering Team hesitated for a moment.
The process would be grim since there were human remains everywhere...
Furthermore, none of them had much experience dismantling machines of this scale.
These machines are too advanced for them.
They might also make mistakes and destroy important parts of them.
However, realizing that Kai and the others would also assist, they immediately felt more confident.
"We... we’re on it, Leader Kai!"
"Let’s go!"
The team moved as they looked at the three Sentinels and two Hounds that were trapped in the collapsed part of the east tunnel.
It was painted red since the blood and fleshly remains of human captives were still present.
However, the smell of the garbage field was stronger...
At this point, they already had a strong stomach that could endure such stench, except for one.
"Ugh..." Claire turned away almost immediately.
Her fists clenched as she couldn’t bear to watch any longer.
The sight of broken bodies tangled in chains and wires was too much.
I’ll help with the traps," she muttered, leaving the salvage to the others.
Kai understood.
He didn’t stop her, since he knew that not everyone could stomach this part of survival.
Furthermore, creating more pit traps or flammable traps was also important.
Just like that, Russel and Augustine also endured the morbid scene as they helped sever the cables and chains that were tied around the Sentinels, previously used to trap their human captives.
For some time, they all worked together dismantling the Sentinels since they were just too heavy.
Dragging them back would also be tough, so they had to at least remove some of their parts.
Then, they could easily transfer them to the warehouse, where they could be further studied.
Of course, there was one of them who would be very useful on this task.
Victor crouched beside a fallen Sentinel, his Adaptive Tinkering skill was already guiding his eyes.
He pointed to a section near the chest cavity.
"We can cut through here.
This should be the Cognitive Processor Unit.
It should be intact if the core didn’t overheat.
We’ll need to cut through the armor."
Well, they had all received the system notifications about the high-value salvageable items within the Sentinels and Hounds.
[ Sentinel’s Salvageable Loot: Cognitive Processor Unit, Targeting Optic Lens, Exo‐Frame Armor Shard, Energy Power Cell, Plasma Rifle ]
[ Hound’s Salvageable Loot: Beastframe Neural Core, Beast Claw Component, Synthetic Muscle Fiber, Hydraulic Joint Cylinder ]
[ Note: Only high‐value salvageable components are listed.
Common debris and low‐grade materials are excluded. ]
Just like that, the salvage began in earnest.
Wallace grunted as he lifted the hand of the Sentinel...
"I’ll hold it steady.
You work and cut it off properly."

"Hurry.
We don’t know how long before the next wave." Ralph reminded.

"Got it," he said while carefully detaching the component.
Then, he got a notification from the system!
[ Item Obtained: Cognitive Processor Unit ]
[ Description: Central processor recovered from Sentinel core that stores combat data and tactical routines. ]

It’s really important...

chapters.title: Chapter 40: Guests
paragraphs: While Kai was looking after the two rescued people, the salvage continued.
In the store room, they pulled an Energy Power Cell from a Sentinel. To their surprise, it was still humming faintly!
"What?!"
"Be careful! It might explode or something!"
Wallace and Ralph couldn’t help but feel worried that it might cause a disaster.
However, Victor’s eyes remained calm.
"It’s alright. This... this is gold. Maybe we can power more devices, maybe even recharge the rifles if I can stabilize the output."
Of course, he wasn’t sure how the rifle worked just yet. Still, he couldn’t help but imagine what he could do with this energy source.
Soon, he looked at the Plasma Rifle.
[ Item Obtained: Plasma Rifle ]
[ Description: A damaged standard‐issue rifle for the Sentinel unit. ]
It was scorched and dented but not destroyed. He lifted it carefully, and it was heavy!
Perhaps, if he didn’t consume the Gene Serum, he would struggle carrying this thing.
Wallace turned to Victor. "Can you fix it?"

Victor examined the rifle. His fingers traced the warped casing. "There are two of them, and they aren’t too badly damaged. With time, I can probably restore them. They’ll be our strongest weapons yet."
"Awesome... Just like what Kai said, prioritize those rifles. They’ll make the difference."
The Hounds were next. They do not have a lot of items they could recover.
’Synthetic muscle fibers... What am I supposed to do with these strings?’’
Although Victor had no idea, he just continued harvesting any usable parts.

Just like that, they gathered the Beast Claw Component that could probably be repurposed into bladed weapons. As for the Hydraulic Joint Cylinder, he could only consider how it could be used to build tools... or even enhance armor’s movement.
At the same time that this was happening, the scouts and other members of the resource-gathering team continued making more traps around the garbage field.
They piled debris, soaked rags in oil, and arranged flammable materials in various areas.
Rene, one of the members of the gatherers team, arranged the soaked rags across a pile of broken chair legs.
At the moment, he wasn’t even wearing a mask as he had grown used to the stench of the garbage field...
Around him, the other members also worked quickly. He saw them drag broken bed frames, plastic scraps, and torn bedding into piles, after soaking them with oil they had scavenged in the scrapyard.
"Spread the grease here," Rene said, pointing to a section of the first trap.
"If the machines come through, the fire will catch faster."
Two men hauled a container of thick, black grease from the shelter’s reserves.
Rene pried open one of the lids and dipped a rag inside, smearing the viscous substance across the debris. The smell was pungent, but he knew it would burn hot.

Soon, they layered plastics over wood, stuffing bedding between cracks, and pouring oil until the trap looked like nothing more than a pile of trash. But he knew the moment fire touched it, the trap would become a furnace.
As he wiped his hands on his trousers, Rene thought of the food he had eaten before...
A few cans of preserved meat from Leader Kai’s storage were a life-changer. It was a luxury for him who had gotten used to eating nuts and leaves.
"Let’s work properly... Leader Kai promised that we’ll have a feast once this ends." Rene reminded the group.
"Yes!" Everyone answered in unison.
With such a motivation, the work was done quickly...
"Alright... That should do it. If they come through here, they’ll regret it." Rene muttered, satisfied with their work.
Then, as they were about to return to the shelter through the hidden tunnel, he noticed some movements from afar...
Rene and the other froze as they realized what was going on!
Six figures were running across the garbage field, stumbling over heaps of twisted metal and broken plastic.
At first, they thought it was another scavenger team returning early. But there were too many of them... Then he saw their clothes.
That color of jacket and pants... They’re the same kind of gear Kai’s group had worn when they were first recruited.
"We have guests!" Rene was shocked.
The others also stared at the approaching figures, their hearts pounding. It was rare to see survivors out here, rarer still to see them running freely.
But then Rene’s eyes caught something else.
Behind the survivors, shadows moved. Tall, metallic silhouettes were following them!
Sentinels.
"Shit! They’re being chased!" he shouted.
The group of survivors stumbled closer, their faces pale...
"Retreat!" Rene ordered, then froze, as he realized something.
"No... wait! If we open the tunnel now, they’ll know where it is!" He was torn between fear and duty.
The others hesitated, glancing at the desperate survivors. The young woman’s cry echoed across the garbage field...
"Help us! Please!"
Rene clenched his jaw. "We can’t save them... Smoke grenades, now! We need to hide the entrance..."
One of the scouts looked at him, horrified. "But... they’re human!"

Rene’s eyes hardened. "We don’t know them. They could be raiders, deserters, or worse... bait sent by the machines. If we gamble on unknowns, we risk all of Haven‐45. Do you want the Sentinels to trace the tunnel back to the shelter?"
The team was stunned, torn between instinct and survival.
Rene reminded them once again.
"They’re not from our shelter..." he said coldly.
"We can’t afford to trust them... Not now."
With those words said, it didn’t take long before the smoke grenades hissed as thick clouds spread across the garbage field.
However, as soon as Rene was able to enter the shelter, he immediately went to Kai, asking for help!

chapters.title: Chapter 41: Charge
paragraphs: As soon as the group of people ran towards their shelter’s area, it was immediately noticed by the scouts monitoring the surroundings.
So even without Rene’s information, Kai was already aware of what was going on.
"Good decision..." Kai muttered after realizing that Rene chose to deploy those smoke grenades.
He then watched as plumes curled across the garbage field through the periscope.
"Six humans... and eight Sentinels, huh."
Kai frowned as he saw the silhouettes of the Sentinels advance. He had no time to hesitate. They need to quickly prepare for battle.
"Wallace, Ralph... revolvers ready. Inform Rene to keep the smoke grenades going. We’ll lure them into the traps." Kai ordered as he also readied himself to join the battle outside.
"At least those Sentinels weren’t carrying human captives." Claire muttered as she looked through the periscope.
"That’s true. We can just focus on shooting them." Victor added.
He had actually just finished analysing some of the materials they looted and had given his report to Kai. He was about to return to the store room when this happened.
"Should I join you?" Victor asked before Kai could leave.
"No need. Just try to make those rifles work... But thanks for the information about the Energy Cell. We can handle this." Kai replied before finally leaving with the team.
Soon, they were outside the underground shelter, hidden behind the smoke created by Rene’s team, who had already retreated.
The fire traps were already primed... There were oil-soaked rags, bedding stuffed into cracks, plastics layered over wood, all smeared with grease.
One spark, and the fire trap would become a furnace.
Through the smoke, Kai saw them... the six survivors. Three men, three women, all of them wore the familiar Tier 1 Survivor Gear, and looking so desperate.
The men had revolvers in their hands while the women carried nothing as they ran as fast as they could.
"Go!" one of the men shouted, pushing the women ahead. "Run through the smoke! Humans are there... A shelter must be nearby! We’ll hold them off!"
Kai frowned as he saw the situation.
They were still too far, so helping them was not possible. Even shooting at the Sentinels could be dangerous and hit the Survivors instead.
They could only watch as the three men turned with their revolvers raised, firing into the advancing Sentinels.
The shots echoed across the garbage field. Soon, they saw sparks flying as bullets struck the Sentinels’ metal body.
For a moment, it seemed they might hold the machines back.
But then the Sentinels raised their rifles and shot a beam of energy!
Thud!
One man fell instantly, his left foot burned through. Another tried moving away, but a second blast dropped him after getting hit on his arm that was holding the revolver.
Soon, the third man screamed and emptied his revolver into a Sentinel’s head casing, but the machine’s armor held.
However, a shot from the advanced rifle stopped him...
"Aacck!"
He was also hit on his arm!
Kai’s jaw clenched.
’Are they planning to capture them?’
He immediately realized that the Sentinels weren’t planning to kill the three. Although they received grievous injuries, they were still alive!
However, if not treated any time soon, those three would die for sure.
In the meantime, the three women stumbled through the smoke and cried...
"Help us!"
"We’ll do anything! Please save Michael! Save them too!"
"I have a Talent that can help with making weapons! Please accept us!"
Kai was already planning to accept them, so he immediately sent Russel to guide the three through the secret tunnel. However, Russel must also guard them, just in case.
"Cover them!" Kai shouted as they made sure to make noise and disrupt the enemies.
Soon, Wallace and Ralph joined him...
At this point, Kai’s mind was already calculating.
Victor had told him just a few moments ago that Sentinel’s rifles had limited energy.
According to the energy cell of the Rifle that they had looted, it could only fire 20 times at maximum energy.
Once the rifles were out of the picture, dealing with the Sentinels would be a lot easier.
"Hold the line," Kai muttered. "Make them waste their fire."
Rene hurled another smoke grenade, and the cloud started thickening.
As they moved within the smoke, the Sentinels fired blindly. Their beams were still slicing through the haze, but it was striking nothing.
Each shot just drained their reserves!
"Draw them in!" Kai shouted.
The team fell back toward the traps, firing their revolvers to bait the machines. The Sentinels followed, while their rifles continued spitting beams.
It was getting more and more dangerous! However, the smoke forced them to move into clearer areas, exactly where Kai wanted them.
"Now!" He shouted as Kai lit the first trap.
Flames roared to life, consuming the pile of plastics and bedding.
Thankfully, three Sentinels stepped directly into the blaze, and it didn’t take that long as the fire consumed them!
The team cheered, seeing that the three were trapped and couldn’t get out.
Unfortunately, there were more of them!
The five other Sentinels who weren’t caught in the trap attacked!
"Keep moving!" Kai reminded.
Wallace fired his revolver, striking a Sentinel’s shoulder joint. Ralph’s shot ricocheted off a casing.
Still, the machines advanced and seemed unstoppable!
However, as they kept firing while using the smoke as a cover, it didn’t take long before the energy rifles of the Sentinels lost their power!
As soon as Kai noticed this, he gave his command!
"Charge!"
