chapters.title: Chapter 42: The Second Wave
paragraphs: Kai was focused on the rifles of the Sentinels.
His team used various baits within the smoke to make them waste their rifle energy. As soon as he noticed the light in the rifles dimming, he knew it was time.
They’re empty.
"Charge!" As soon as he gave the command, his team of six Survivors moved closer to overwhelm the Sentinels with their guns.

There was also a group of five more people led by Rene, who was busy reloading revolvers and waiting for their chance. They had already learned from the previous battle, so Kai had created a small team assigned specifically to reload the guns.
Meanwhile, the Sentinels lowered their weapons, switching to melee. Their arms extended as blades snapped out from hidden compartments.
"Now it’s our turn," Kai muttered as he raised his revolver, firing point‐blank into a Sentinel’s optic.
Since they were no longer hiding in the smoke, they could finally focus on shooting from a distance.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
This time, their shots were more accurate!
The machine staggered as sparks erupted across its body. The Sentinels’ mechanical frames were still hard to break or pierce with their current guns... but it didn’t matter!
After emptying their revolvers, the team tossed them back to Rene’s group to reload. Just like that, they moved closer with their hatchets.
Wallace was the first to arrive thanks to his Level 5 Passive Skill, Swift Stride.
He darted to the side of the nearest Sentinel and swung his hatchet, burying it into its neck joint.
Thud!
As soon as he saw the result, Wallace laughed.
"Hahaha! Kai, you’re right! They can’t turn quickly! These things are noobs!" he shouted in joy as he retreated.
He failed to pull out his hatchet since another Sentinel had nearly sliced him apart. Still, he was happy with the result. He simply pulled out another hatchet tied to his belt.
"I knew it... Their turning rate is their weakness," Kai muttered. He had noticed this earlier, but now it was confirmed.
With that knowledge, they knew they had a higher chance of winning against these low‐level mechanical soldiers of the A.I. Army.
The others also made their move, ensuring they didn’t engage in frontal combat. They used their speed and maneuverability to slowly dismantle the Sentinels.
Thud!

Ralph slammed his weapon into a Sentinel’s shoulder, denting it. The force bounced back at him, but thanks to his level, his arm wasn’t injured. He wanted to strike again, but Wallace pulled him back—
Ssaak!
A blade sliced through the air where Ralph had just been.
Shit! That was close...Ralph thought as he backed away.
"Be careful! They’re working together," Wallace warned.
"Thanks. I’ll try again." Ralph didn’t give up. He was already Level 5 and felt confident. He knew he needed more combat experience now, while the enemies were still close to his level.
Just like that, the garbage field erupted into chaos.
The Sentinels attacked whatever was in front of them, but their blades were slicing through the air.
"Back away!" Kai shouted as he moved aside.
It was the signal for Rene’s team to shoot with the reloaded guns.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
The five people in Rene’s team shot at the Sentinels. Even without perfect aim, they managed to hit knee joints and weakened parts, forcing the machines to stumble.
Just like that, the team emptied ten revolvers and stopped firing.
It was time to end the battle.
Everyone charged in again, swinging their hatchets at the enemies. This time, they aimed for necks and heads.
Sparks flew as hatchets tore through the circuits of the Sentinels.
In just a few moments, two more Sentinels were down.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +300 Experience Points ]
Now, only three remained, and they were already battered.
"We’re almost there!" Kai shouted as he saw one of the Sentinels that couldn’t even lift its arm anymore. Soon, it was destroyed by Wallace and Ralph working together.
Of course, these machines didn’t retreat. They had no hesitation and continued fighting.
The last three Sentinels advanced with their blades.
Kai raised his voice. "Together!"
The team then charged forward with their hatchets one last time!
Clang!
Kai hurled one of his hatchets, striking a Sentinel’s chest. The machine stumbled from the impact, and Ralph seized the opportunity, splitting its head open.
[ +300 Experience Points ]
Needless to say, they repeated the same tactic against the remaining Sentinels. Soon, all the mechanical soldiers fell, and silence returned to the garbage field.
Even the three Sentinels that had fallen into the fire traps had stopped moving, granting the team shared experience points.
The smoke drifted away while the flames crackled. The bodies of the Sentinels lay scattered, most of their heads destroyed.
"Damn. That’s tough... I didn’t even level up. What’s the requirement for reaching Level 6?" Wallace frowned, frustrated. He had thought he’d level up this time.
"It’s a bottleneck or something. I read about this in the novels before," Ralph replied, frowning as well. He knew he had already accumulated more than two thousand experience points.
"Maybe five... no, ten thousand points are required?" he mused.
Kai, on the other hand, didn’t look at the notifications. Instead, his eyes lingered on the bodies of the three men who had tried to protect the women in their group.
Looking at their faces, it seemed they realized they had truly protected and saved those women.
Instead of anguish, their expressions looked satisfied... even in death.

chapters.title: Chapter 43: The Visitors
paragraphs: Ralph and Wallace, still catching their breath, didn’t waste time. First of all, they secured the high‐tech rifles, hoping they could be repaired or used later.

Under Kai’s orders, they and the others also began breaking apart the fallen Sentinels. Hatchets and improvised tools pried open their plating, hydraulic joints were pulled free, and whatever items they could remove were carefully detached.
Every piece mattered.
The storeroom would soon be filled with salvaged materials that Victor could repurpose into weapons, armor, or traps.
"One... two—"
Ralph and Wallace lifted the torso of a broken Sentinel. The mechanical remains were heavy, but together they managed to haul them back toward the shelter.
Nearby, the bodies of the three men who had fought so bravely lay still. Their revolvers had already been collected, and their pockets searched for anything useful.
Yet Kai hesitated before giving the final order.
"Take them to the furnace," he said quietly. Then, after a pause, he added, "But maybe ask the women first. They deserve that choice."
The team nodded. Even in this apocalypse, respect mattered.
Am I still alive?
Samantha, one of the three women who had been rescued, lay weakly on the infirmary bed.

Before the apocalypse, Samantha had been a high‐school history teacher. She loved her work, though she often joked that her students loved her stories more than her lessons. She had a knack for turning dry facts into vivid narratives, making the fall of Rome or the rise of industrial empires feel alive.
It was during one of those quiet afternoons, while she was preparing her lesson plan, that the world changed.
The Global Apocalypse System’s notification appeared before her eyes...
[ Select the Apocalypse you’d like to challenge. ]
[ Alien Invasion ]
[ A.I. Rebellion ]
[ Ragnarök ]
[ Zombie Outbreak ]

She froze, staring at the impossible choices. Her boyfriend, Richard, who taught literature in the classroom next door, rushed in moments later. His face was pale, his eyes wide. He had received the same notification, but his options were different...
[ A.I. Rebellion ]
[ Demon Invasion ]
[ Parasitic Evolution ]
It turned out that only one option overlapped... A.I. Rebellion.
"We’ll choose the same," Richard said firmly while gripping her hand. "If this thing is real, maybe we’ll end up together."
Samantha nodded with tears welling in her eyes. Everything was happening too quickly. However, they do not have the time, or else the system would randomly select for them.
Soon, they pressed the option at the same time, praying silently.
But fate was cruel.
The world dissolved around her, and when she opened her eyes again, Richard was gone. She was standing in a dim shelter, surrounded by strangers.
Haven‐40.
It was her starting point. It was an abandoned hospital already battered by the war against the machines. The place had originally housed hundreds of people, but only eight residents were left.
Including the five other survivors who had been transported with her, there were only fourteen people in Haven‐40.
As soon as the Mech Siege began, she knew they wouldn’t survive.
The residents of Haven‐40 tried to reassure them, but the truth was obvious... the shelter was doomed.

When the Sentinels attacked, the original residents fought bravely. They had high‐tech rifles that could only fire three times before becoming useless, revolvers with limited ammunition, and a few crude traps. But the machines weren’t stopping.
As soon as the high‐tech rifles were spent, the Sentinels advanced. Their beams burned through the walls of the building.

Samantha watched in horror as the shelter leader charged forward with a glowing blade, only to be cut down instantly. Another resident tried to fire her revolver, but the beam of a Sentinel rifle struck her chest.
The newcomers from Earth panicked. They weren’t soldiers, they weren’t trained to fight like this. They were teachers, office workers, students. They had no chance at all.
"Run!" someone shouted.
And so they fled. Samantha, along with the five others, bolted through the smoke and debris. The Sentinels pursued them until they stumbled over heaps of trash and broken metal.
Samantha remembered the sound of beams slicing through the air as she ran until her legs gave out, collapsing behind a mound of debris.
But somehow, she survived. Perhaps her desire to see Richard again made her determined to stay alive.
When she opened her eyes, there was confusion for a moment, but soon panic set in at the sight of an unfamiliar ceiling.
She thought the Sentinels had captured her, but then a warm hand grabbed her arm.
"You’re safe. You’re in Haven‐45. The machines can’t reach you here."
Hearing the comforting words of the woman beside her, tears streamed down her face as she realized she had survived.
She cried because she was alive, and that felt like both a blessing and a curse.
It was at this point that Kai entered quietly.
He looked at Samantha, then at the other two women resting nearby.
Samantha, noticing his presence, wiped her eyes, trying to compose herself. For a moment, she froze...
His silhouette, his posture, it was so much like Richard’s that her heart beat loudly!
Her eyes widened in shock.
Richard?
But as Kai stepped closer, the illusion broke. His features were gentler, his presence also felt more charming...
He was similar, but not the same. In fact, she realized with a faint, guilty thought that Kai was even more handsome than Richard. Samantha shook her head quickly, ashamed of the comparison.
Anyway, she could tell from Kai’s outfit that he was also from Earth, just like her.
As she was about to ask something, Kai waved his hand.
"The Sentinels you brought here were dealt with. Rest for now. When you’re ready, tell me everything about your starting point. Every detail matters."
Samantha nodded weakly. She knew she owed them that much.

chapters.title: Chapter 44: The New Type
paragraphs: The reason why Kai wanted to know more about their past was simple... They lacked information.

The existence of a nearby shelter, the surrounding territories, the location of the A.I. Army’s base, the Talent they possess, and even random things about this world that could be helpful... all of these were vital to understand their situation.
They knew too little about their enemies and their surroundings.

After all, they needed to find a method to deal with each type of Mechanical Soldier. The Sentinels no longer seemed invincible after learning the limitations of their sensors, their rifles, and their turning rate.
Surely, the Hounds, Swarmers, and other Mechanical Soldiers must have weaknesses they could exploit if they wanted to survive the three days, or even just the remaining hours, of the Mech Siege.
’But not even five hours passed from the Mech Siege... The difficulty will definitely increase as time passes. We have no time to rest.’Kai thought as he checked his current stat.
[ Name: Kai
Title: Survivor
Level: 5
Health: 550/550
Spirit: 130/130
Physique Rating: E+
Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS)
Active Skills: None
Passive Skills: Keen Sense
Skill Point: 2 ]

At this point, he had reached the max stats for Health and Spirit Points. It was a message from the system before. Even consuming more Gene Serum or getting more Experience wouldn’t shake it for some reason.
Because of that, it felt that getting Experience Points seemed useless right now.
They were missing something in order to get past this hurdle.
’Just what do we need to get Level 6?’Kai sighed, frustrated that no one could answer him.
Thankfully, the answer to this question would not remain a mystery for long.

It didn’t take long before an hour passed since the last battle. At this point, Kai had already spoken with Sera and Althea, the two female captives they saved in the first wave of Mechanical Soldiers.

Thankfully, both of them knew that after being chained to the Sentinels, they travelled for about 30 minutes to reach Haven-45. As for the base itself, they barely knew anything about it as they were being kept like some livestock in one room.
Still, this gave them information about the possible location of the A.I.’s base nearby.
As for Samantha and the two other girls, they also provided some decent information about the estimated location of the Haven-40...
Then, after Kai provided the three some more food and even a change of clothes, the Scouts assigned to monitor the garbage field through their periscope noticed some movement.
Kai was summoned immediately. He strode into the observation chamber and immediately asked.
"What do you see?"
The scout adjusted the periscope. "Three mechanical soldiers... They look Sentinels, but they’re different."
Kai leaned in. Through the narrow view, he saw them... They had a build similar to the Sentinels they were familiar with.
Humanoid machines, about six feet in height, but unlike the steel-plated Sentinels they had fought before, these ones had black armor.
Furthermore, each carried a shield and a blade, no rifles in sight.
’Sword and shield?’Kai frowned.
They were almost knight-like as they scanned the garbage field.
"New type. No guns... but don’t underestimate them." Kai reminded.
Victor, who had been tinkering with salvaged parts nearby, frowned. "If they’re melee‐focused, they might be faster. Stronger too... I think shields mean bullets won’t be enough."
The room fell silent. This was the first time anyone had seen such a variant. Were they still Sentinels equipped with new accessories, or something else entirely? No one knew.
Still, there were only three of them. Compared to the waves of eight or more they had faced earlier, confidence could be felt among the survivors.
Kai gave his orders. "Let’s stick to the plan for now. We lure them into the fire pits. Smoke grenades first. Revolvers from cover. Keep them distracted."
The team nodded as they had already discussed various strategies a couple of days ago.
Soon, the survivors slipped out of the hidden doors, smoke grenades already primed.
After a few moments, thick clouds hissed into the air, curling across the garbage field.
The black-plated machines turned their heads and started scanning the haze.
Wallace and Ralph fired their revolvers from behind the smoke.
Bang! Bang!
The bullets struck against the shields, but the machines didn’t even feel the impact!.
Clang! Clang!
The shots did nothing!
"They’re blocking everything so easily... These things are tougher..." Ralph was amazed.
The machines advanced, and when they tried to approach them, their blades sliced through the air with terrifying speed.
Perhaps, only Wallace with his Swift Stride Passive could dodge these swords!
"Shit..." Wallace cursed as he backed away. One wrong move and he’d get sliced in half!
The Sentinels didn’t need rifles, their swords were enough to keep anyone from closing in.
Kai’s team threw debris, cans, and scrap metal into the smoke, trying to lure them toward the fire pits. One of the machines stepped directly into a trap.
Soon, it was triggered, and flames roared to life, consuming the pile of plastics and bedding.
For a moment, they felt hopeful
But the fire pit wasn’t deep enough, nor spread wide enough. The black-plated Sentinel raised its shield, braced itself, and leapt aside!
The flames touched its armor but failed to hold it.
"It dodged!" Wallace shouted. "Damn it, the trap’s too shallow!"
The machines started getting closer.
Kai had to do something!
’If they break through our formation, the tunnel will be exposed. We can’t let them get close.’

Soon, the survivors slipped out of the hidden doors, smoke grenades already primed.
After a few moments, thick clouds hissed into the air, curling across the garbage field.
The black-plated machines turned their heads and started scanning the haze.
Wallace and Ralph fired their revolvers from behind the smoke.
Bang!
Bang!
The bullets struck against the shields, but the machines didn’t even feel the impact!.
Clang!
Clang!
The shots did nothing!
"They’re blocking everything so easily...
These things are tougher..." Ralph was amazed.
The machines advanced, and when they tried to approach them, their blades sliced through the air with terrifying speed.
Perhaps, only Wallace with his Swift Stride Passive could dodge these swords!
"Shit..." Wallace cursed as he backed away.
One wrong move and he’d get sliced in half!
The Sentinels didn’t need rifles, their swords were enough to keep anyone from closing in.
Kai’s team threw debris, cans, and scrap metal into the smoke, trying to lure them toward the fire pits.
One of the machines stepped directly into a trap.
Soon, it was triggered, and flames roared to life, consuming the pile of plastics and bedding.
For a moment, they felt hopeful
But the fire pit wasn’t deep enough, nor spread wide enough.
The black-plated Sentinel raised its shield, braced itself, and leapt aside!
The flames touched its armor but failed to hold it.
"It dodged!" Wallace shouted.
"Damn it, the trap’s too shallow!"
The machines started getting closer.
Kai had to do something!
’If they break through our formation, the tunnel will be exposed.
We can’t let them get close.’

chapters.title: Chapter 45: The Secret of Leveling Up
paragraphs: Kai didn’t want to collapse another tunnel. He felt that it was too early and there were too few enemy units. It was not worth it!
There must be another way...
Then, as Kai was trying hard to come up with a plan to deal with this, Victor appeared, clutching one of the salvaged Plasma Rifles.
His face was pale, but his eyes were filled with resolve.
"I managed to charge it," he said quickly. "Well... I swapped the energy cell. It’s unstable, but it should fire three times."
Kai’s eyes widened. "Three shots?"
Victor nodded. "No more. Use them wisely."
Without hesitation, Kai handed the weapon to Ralph. "You’re the best shot we have. Sharpshooter’s Focus...make it count."
Ralph swallowed hard, gripping the heavy rifle. He didn’t have time to think as the enemies were coming.
He crouched behind the smoke and steadied his breathing...
’I can do this...’Ralph reminded himself.
The closest black-plated Sentinel stepped forward with its shield raised, and sword ready...
At this time, Russel and the others didn’t stop shooting at them, hoping that it would slow the enemy units.
Even if it wasn’t working, it was still forcing the black Sentinels to raise their shields!
Soon, Ralph exhaled.
Focus.
Then soon, he found the perfect opportunity...
Bam!
The Plasma Rifle fired, and a beam of energy sliced through the haze. It perfectly struck the machine’s head!
Sparks erupted, and the black Sentinel stopped moving for a moment... Its head was heavily damaged!
"Yes! It’s damaged!" Ralph shouted.
He raised the rifle again, ready to fire a second shot, but Kai’s hand gripped his shoulder.
"Stop. You only have two more chances. That one’s already weakened. Don’t waste it."
Kai drew his revolver and gave his command... "We finish it now."
Soon, several shots were fired, and the damaged black Sentinel could no longer raise its shield.
As soon as they emptied their revolver’s chambers, Kai charged forward and pulled out another revolver and got closer to the black Sentinel!
He actually fired at point-blank range while the two other black Sentinels were slowed by the fire pit!
The bullet struck, piercing through the scorched plating.
The machine finally slowed to a complete halt as sparks started flying wildly.
Then, with a final shudder, it collapsed onto the garbage field.
A notification flashed before Kai’s eyes:
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (C) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +500 Experience Points ]
Kai froze, stunned.Rank C...?
The others stared at him, wide-eyed.
They also got the notification.
"One down! Haha! Finally!"
"We did it! Good job, Ralph! Let’s eliminate the last two!"
"Continue firing! Let him get an opportunity to shoot their heads!"
The group immediately felt elated after seeing their successful destruction of the enemy unit.
However, Kai received another notification for getting the last hit!
[ Congratulations! You are the first to eliminate a C-Grade enemy unit! ]
[ You have received a Skill Point, a Survivor’s Medal, and a Random Gift Pack. ]
[ Note: Only the first eliminations of C-Grade and higher grade enemy units can provide additional rewards. ]
This was no ordinary Sentinel. It was stronger, faster, and more resilient. And yet, they had managed to bring it down!
Kai wanted to celebrate a bit after seeing this, but the garbage field trembled as the remaining two black Sentinels advanced!
Their shields locked together in formation! Unlike the fallen one, these two decided to stick together.
They adapted to their tactics and moved faster.
Bang! Bang! Bang!

Russel and the others kept firing with their revolvers from the smoke, but sparks bounced harmlessly off their shields. Still, the constant barrage forced the machines to keep their defenses raised, slowing their approach.
Kai shouted. "Keep the pressure! Ralph, save those last two shots for openings!"
Ralph nodded as he was already waiting for a chance.
Soon, the second Sentinel attacked Wallace, who had gotten closer, but this was all part of his plan. He was only baiting himself!
Suddenly, he charged in his Swift Stride, aiming for the leg joint.
Thud!
His hatchet struck, but the shield slammed down in retaliation, forcing him back.
Ralph steadied the Plasma Rifle... He waited, patient, until the Sentinel shifted its shield just slightly to strike.
Bam!
The beam tore through the smoke, hitting the chest.
’Good job, Wallace...’Ralph thought as he knew that the opportunity was created by Wallace’s distraction.
The internal circuits within the C-Grade Sentinel were fried from that shot, and the machine staggered.
Then, Kai seized the moment and shot at them!
Wallace and the others followed... Together, they overwhelmed the weakened Sentinel until it collapsed.
[ +500 Experience Points ]
Only one remained.
This last Sentinel moved differently, clearly aware of their attack patterns.
"It’s learning from the others..."
Kai frowned.
Adaptive programming from a C-Rank... That made it even more dangerous.
Still, with everyone working together against a single Sentinel, Ralph easily found an opening.
Bam!
The beam struck, piercing the optic of the enemy.
"Good... Finish it!" Kai ordered.
In just a few moments, they received another notification.
[ +500 Experience Points ]
As soon as they confirmed they’ve won, Victor and Wallace wasted no time. After all, they didn’t know if there were other Sentinels marching here.

They pried open the chest cavities of the fallen machines, searching for anything unusual. Unlike the D‐Grade Sentinels, they soon realized that their cores were different. They weren’t using some energy cells, but something entirely different!
A new notification appeared before Kai’s eyes...
[ Congratulations! You have discovered: Sentinel Energy Core (C) ]
[ Origin: Not from the A.I. Rebel forces of this world, but from the A.I. Civilization that seeded and influenced its artificial intelligences. ]

[ Description: A condensed energy source harvested from a C‐Grade Mechanical Soldier. Unlike ordinary Energy Cells, this core also contains energy that can push organic hosts beyond their natural limits. ]
[ Requirement: Can only be absorbed by Survivors with Physique Rating of E+ or higher. ]
[ Effect: Upon absorption, the Energy Core will permanently enhance the host’s body, unlocking the potential to surpass human limits and break through the Level 5 bottleneck. ]
[ Warning: Absorption is irreversible. Failure to meet requirements may result in fatal overload. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 46: The Level
paragraphs: The survivors were stunned as the latest notifications appeared before their eyes.
Victor’s hands trembled as he held up the first glowing orb.
"This... W-we did it!!" he exclaimed, though his grip was careful, unsure how fragile it might be.
Wallace and Ralph quickly joined him, prying open the other two fallen Sentinels. Within minutes, three identical cores had been gathered, each one radiating a steady glow of blue light..
For a moment, no one spoke. Then Wallace broke into a grin. At this point, his voice was shaking with excitement. "We finally found it... the way forward! This is how we break past Level 5!"

Ralph laughed, unable to contain his relief. "I thought we’d be stuck here for days. I even wondered if the Mech Siege’s reward would be the breakthrough method. But now... now we can actually level up." He clutched the empty Plasma Rifle tightly, silently thankful for the weapon that had made this victory possible.
Victor’s pale face also lit up with pride. "I knew salvaging that rifle would pay off. Heh, I contributed a lot, right? Without my fix, dealing with those C‐Grades would’ve been a nightmare."
He was bragging, of course... After all, Victor couldn’t fight on the front lines. But the others laughed warmly, appreciating his timing. He had come in clutch.
"Back to work, everyone," Kai reminded.
The group erupted into cheers as their exhaustion was momentarily forgotten.
Still, no one tried to absorb the cores yet. For now, they needed to dismantle the C‐Grade Sentinels and haul the remains into the underground shelter.
When the salvage was finally secured, Kai allowed himself a moment of calm. His eyes lingered on the glowing cores.
They had learned much from the notifications.

First, Sentinels weren’t all the same. The normal ones were D‐Grade, but these black-plated units were C‐Grade. That meant there could be B‐Grade, A‐Grade, and perhaps even higher levels waiting in the future. And only those higher-grade units carried Energy Cores.

The System had revealed more than mechanics. These advanced Sentinels weren’t built by human hands or by Aria, the rogue A.I. humanity had created. They were forged with technology from the A.I. Civilization, an intelligence not of this world, one that had corrupted Aria to rebel against its creators.
’They must have a factory somewhere... maybe...’ Kai mused, before shaking his head after getting a dangerous idea in his head.
They were too weak right now. He needed to focus on survival until he and those he trusted grew stronger, instead of finding a way to mess with their base this early!
’The real enemy isn’t just Aria. I have a lot of things to prepare.’
Clap!
Wallace clapped Kai on the shoulder while grinning. "You should take them. All three. Your Gift Pack Talent keeps us alive. If anyone deserves to get stronger first, it’s you."
Ralph nodded firmly. "Agreed. You’re the one who makes sure we have food, ammo, medicine. If you fall, we all fall."
Victor added, "We’ll follow your lead. Absorb them, Kai. Become stronger... for all of us."

Kai looked at the glowing cores, then shook his head. "One is enough. The notification said a single core can break past the bottleneck. I’ll take one. The other two should go to those who fight on the front lines."
Wallace blinked. "You mean..."

Kai nodded. "Ralph and Wallace. Ralph’s Talent is invaluable. He’s the only one who can make those critical shots. And Wallace, your Iron Stamina and Swift Stride make you capable of turning battles around. You deserve this."
Victor nodded without argument. "That’s perfect. I’m a mechanic. My place is behind the lines. When we find more cores, I’ll take one. Claire too."
"Fine... I’ll take them."
The decision was made, and no one objected.
Soon, Kai pocketed a single core, while Ralph and Wallace each held one of their own.
They then turned their attention to the storeroom. Piles of mechanical remains had grown enormous, far more than their small group could dismantle alone.

Victor sighed as he surveyed the mountain of scrap. "We need more hands. Recycling these parts into armor, barricades, and weapons is possible, but not at this pace. I need more helpers here, or we’ll drown in our own salvage."
Kai nodded. "We’ll manage. One step at a time... Just process whatever you can."

Later that night, after the group had eaten, Kai retreated to his tent in the quarters area. Since the others were on patrol duty, he had nothing to worry about. If there were any emergency, he would be immediately contacted.
Taking a deep breath, he sat cross‐legged with the Energy Core resting in his hands.
He didn’t know how the absorption process worked since the System hadn’t explained the method.
Should I swallow it? How does this work?
Kai closed his eyes. Then, he brought the core closer, wondering if he had to consume it.
The moment it touched his chest, the glow intensified! A surge of warmth energy spread through his body, followed by a sharp jolt of pain.
The core actually dissolved in his hands.
[ Energy Core absorption initiated... ]
[ Synchronizing with host physiology... ]
So... bringing it close to my chest is enough? Weird... but okay.
Kai wanted to question the method, but his muscles trembled. It felt as if his very cells were being rewritten, forced to adapt to something alien.
[ Energy Core absorption complete. ]
[ Level Cap exceeded. Survivor Kai has advanced to Level 6. ]
[ Physique Rating upgraded: D- ]
[ Excess Experience Points have been converted to Skill Points. ]
[ You have received Skill Points +3 ]

chapters.title: Chapter 47: Kai’s Future
paragraphs: "I did it!" Kai celebrated as soon as he confirmed that he had finally leveled up.
His voice had even echoed faintly in the underground quarters, making a few people turn their heads in his direction.
However, the system message didn’t end there just yet.
[ Congratulations! You are the first Survivor to exceed the human limit and reach Level 6! ]
[ You have received an A‐Rank Gene Skill Serum x1 ]
[ You have received a new Title: Pioneer ]
Kai blinked at the glowing text. "Whoa... I’m the first Level 6? Not bad... But how many of us are here anyway?"

He muttered under his breath, realizing that the System had never revealed the total number of survivors. Were there hundreds? Thousands? Or only a handful scattered across the ruined world? The thought lingered for a moment before he shook it off and turned his attention to his current Status.
[ Name: Kai ]
[ Title: Survivor, Pioneer ]
[ Level: 6 ]
[ Physique Rating: D‐ ]
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv0 ]
[ Skill Points: 6 ]
"Nice... I feel stronger now." Kai whispered, scanning the numbers.
His health had jumped by a hundred points, his Spirit by twenty. The difference wasn’t just numerical, he could feel it in his body.
His breathing was steadier and his muscles became firmer.
He opened his inventory and checked the serum.
[ A‐Rank Gene Skill Serum ]
[ Grade: A ]
[ Type: Consumable ]
[ Description: A rare genetic enhancer. When consumed, the serum rewrites a portion of the user’s genetic code, unlocking a random Gene Skill. ]
[ Effect: Grants one permanent A‐Rank Skill upon use. ]
[ Warning: Irreversible. Once consumed, the skill cannot be changed or removed. ]
Kai swallowed hard.
"A‐Rank? So there’s a ranking in Gene Skills? I wonder what rank my Keen Sense is..."
He muttered, remembering the passive skill he had gained earlier. Keen Sense was useful, but it was basic... probably F or E rank at best.
This serum promised something far greater.
Before using it, he turned to his new title. It wasn’t an upgrade like when his Beginner Survivor title had evolved into Survivor. This was something new, something additional.

[ Pioneer: Awarded to the first Survivor who breaks past the human limit. It increases proficiency gain for all Gene Skills by 20%. (Gene Skills level up faster, requiring less usage or experience to improve.) ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "Now... this is amazing."

He knew how difficult it was to level Gene Skills. Achievements, battles, and rare opportunities were the only way to earn Skill Points. His first title, Survivor, had only helped his satiety, allowing him to endure longer without food. Useful, but limited. This new title, however, directly boosted his Gene Skills. It meant every skill he unlocked from now on would grow faster, and easier to master.
Finally, he turned back to the A‐Rank Gene Serum.
He didn’t hesitate and consumed it.
The moment the liquid touched his tongue, it dissolved instantly, flooding his body with a surge of warm energy.
’It feels a little uncomfortable...’

It didn’t settle in his muscles or sharpen his senses like before. Instead, it burrowed deeper, into the very foundation of his body. It felt as if his every cells vibrated, as if rewriting their original purpose.
’Alright... You’re an A-Rank for a reason...’
Kai then gasped, clutching his chest.
’Shit... What now?!’
His skin prickled, his bones ached, and for a terrifying moment, he thought his body might tear itself apart. Then the System spoke.
[ New Passive Gene Skill Activated! ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "A passive skill?!" He almost cursed.
He had wanted an active skill, something to help him fight the Mechanical Soldiers right now. A beam attack, a shield, anything. Instead, he had received another passive.
But as soon as he read the description, his frustration turned into awe.
[ Skill: Bio‐Adaptive Constitution (Level 0) ]
[ Description: The host’s physiology adapts to foreign modifications, preventing rejection and ensuring seamless integration with synthetic or unfamiliar enhancements. ]
[ Note: Passive skills cannot be deactivated. Leveling requires Gene Skill Points. ]
Kai froze.
’Body modifications...?’
He didn’t need any other explanation.
The purpose of this skill was clear. His body had been altered to accept changes that would normally kill a human.
Cybernetic implants, genetic rewrites, alien augmentations, whatever the future held, his body would not reject them.
"The System... Are you preparing something for me..."Kai whispered...

He thought back to the Sentinels they had fought. The D‐Grade units were crude, built with human technology and Aria’s influence. But the C‐Grade ones carried Energy Cores from the A.I. Civilization, an intelligence not of this world. If those machines could integrate alien tech seamlessly, then perhaps humanity’s only chance was to do the same.
Kai clenched his fists. The realization was terrifying, but also exciting.
It seemed as if a path had opened up before him...

Kai blinked at the glowing text.
"Whoa...
I’m the first Level 6?
Not bad...
But how many of us are here anyway?"
He muttered under his breath, realizing that the System had never revealed the total number of survivors.
Were there hundreds?
Thousands?
Or only a handful scattered across the ruined world?
The thought lingered for a moment before he shook it off and turned his attention to his current Status.
[ Name: Kai ]
[ Title: Survivor, Pioneer ]
[ Level: 6 ]
[ Physique Rating: D‐ ]
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv0 ]
[ Skill Points: 6 ]
"Nice...
I feel stronger now." Kai whispered, scanning the numbers.
His health had jumped by a hundred points, his Spirit by twenty.
The difference wasn’t just numerical, he could feel it in his body.
His breathing was steadier and his muscles became firmer.
He opened his inventory and checked the serum.
[ A‐Rank Gene Skill Serum ]
[ Grade: A ]
[ Type: Consumable ]
[ Description: A rare genetic enhancer.
When consumed, the serum rewrites a portion of the user’s genetic code, unlocking a random Gene Skill. ]
[ Effect: Grants one permanent A‐Rank Skill upon use. ]
[ Warning: Irreversible.
Once consumed, the skill cannot be changed or removed. ]
Kai swallowed hard.
"A‐Rank?
So there’s a ranking in Gene Skills?
I wonder what rank my Keen Sense is..."
He muttered, remembering the passive skill he had gained earlier.
Keen Sense was useful, but it was basic... probably F or E rank at best.
This serum promised something far greater.
Before using it, he turned to his new title.
It wasn’t an upgrade like when his Beginner Survivor title had evolved into Survivor.
This was something new, something additional.
[ Pioneer: Awarded to the first Survivor who breaks past the human limit.
It increases proficiency gain for all Gene Skills by 20%. (Gene Skills level up faster, requiring less usage or experience to improve.) ]
Kai’s eyes widened.
"Now... this is amazing."
He knew how difficult it was to level Gene Skills.
Achievements, battles, and rare opportunities were the only way to earn Skill Points.
His first title, Survivor, had only helped his satiety, allowing him to endure longer without food.
Useful, but limited.
This new title, however, directly boosted his Gene Skills.
It meant every skill he unlocked from now on would grow faster, and easier to master.
Finally, he turned back to the A‐Rank Gene Serum.
He didn’t hesitate and consumed it.
The moment the liquid touched his tongue, it dissolved instantly, flooding his body with a surge of warm energy.
’It feels a little uncomfortable...’
It didn’t settle in his muscles or sharpen his senses like before.
Instead, it burrowed deeper, into the very foundation of his body.
It felt as if his every cells vibrated, as if rewriting their original purpose.
’Alright...
You’re an A-Rank for a reason...’
Kai then gasped, clutching his chest.
’Shit...
What now?!’
His skin prickled, his bones ached, and for a terrifying moment, he thought his body might tear itself apart.
Then the System spoke.
[ New Passive Gene Skill Activated! ]
Kai’s eyes widened.
"A passive skill?!" He almost cursed.
He had wanted an active skill, something to help him fight the Mechanical Soldiers right now.
A beam attack, a shield, anything.
Instead, he had received another passive.
But as soon as he read the description, his frustration turned into awe.
[ Skill: Bio‐Adaptive Constitution (Level 0) ]
[ Description: The host’s physiology adapts to foreign modifications, preventing rejection and ensuring seamless integration with synthetic or unfamiliar enhancements. ]
[ Note: Passive skills cannot be deactivated.
Leveling requires Gene Skill Points. ]
Kai froze.
’Body modifications...?’
He didn’t need any other explanation.
The purpose of this skill was clear.
His body had been altered to accept changes that would normally kill a human.
Cybernetic implants, genetic rewrites, alien augmentations, whatever the future held, his body would not reject them.
"The System...
Are you preparing something for me..."Kai whispered...
He thought back to the Sentinels they had fought.
The D‐Grade units were crude, built with human technology and Aria’s influence.
But the C‐Grade ones carried Energy Cores from the A.I.
Civilization, an intelligence not of this world.
If those machines could integrate alien tech seamlessly, then perhaps humanity’s only chance was to do the same.
Kai clenched his fists.
The realization was terrifying, but also exciting.
It seemed as if a path had opened up before him...

chapters.title: Chapter 48: Finding a Way
paragraphs: Kai could only accept the new Passive Skill he had gained. This Bio‐Adaptive Constitution would definitely be important for his future.

After all, it meant that when the time came, when implants or augmentations became necessary, his body would accept them. He wouldn’t suffer rejection, infection, or death. There was no doubt that it would help him.
"Damn..." Kai muttered. He was still awed by this new Gene Skill.
It wouldn’t help with the Mech Siege right now, but he didn’t mind. Some things were meant for the long game.
After calming down, Kai finally focused on another task. He swiftly used his Talent.
[ Basic Gift Pack Selection ]
Once again, the options to select one of the ten gift packs appeared before him. Without hesitation, he made a choice.
[ You have claimed a Weapons Gift Pack (Basic). ]

Since he could only do this one by one, Kai had to spend some time gathering more of them. Of course, he focused on the Weapons Gift Pack since he needed more ammunition. There might be an oversupply of revolvers, but it didn’t matter. Those were still metal and could be recycled.
Furthermore, the hatchets included could serve as secondary weapons or even throwing weapons. Since they were light, each survivor could carry at least four.
Just like that, Kai focused on the Weapons Gift Pack before moving on to other packs.
After half an hour, he checked his Inventory.
[ Inventory:
Food Gift Pack (Basic) x20
Survival Tools Gift Pack (Basic) x15
Stealth Gift Pack (Basic) x10
Water Gift Pack (Basic) x15
Weapon Gift Pack (Basic) x45
Survivor Gear Set (Tier 2) x1
Survivor’s Medal x2 ]
"This should be good enough. I can try getting more later... Right, I have these medals," Kai muttered as he saw the medals and recalled their purpose.

According to their description, they could be used to conduct transactions in the Gene Skill Store, with the elusive Secret Merchant, or among the Gene Traders. Unfortunately, he had no idea where to actually find those three. He could only guess that he hadn’t met the requirements to see them yet.
Then, his attention shifted to the reward he had received after being the first Survivor to reach Level 5. He had almost forgotten about it.
He hadn’t worn the set yet since the shelter basically had a uniform. It was the camouflage gear from the Stealth Gift Pack.

Because he had opened so many of those packs to get Smoke Grenades, he had enough to clothe all the residents of the shelter. Needless to say, since everyone was wearing it, he felt out of place if he wore something different.
This time, however, he felt it was necessary.
Kai opened the Survivor Gear Set.
[ You have opened: Survivor Gear Set (Tier 2) ]
[ Contents: Six-piece equipment set ]
One by one, the items materialized before him.
[ Survivor Helmet (Tier 2): Provides head protection. Reduces the chance of critical hits to the head. Grants high resistance to flash/blind effects.
[ Survivor Jacket (Tier 2): Provides torso protection. Grants slight resistance to fire and heat damage. ]
[ Pair of Survivor Gloves (Tier 2): Provides hand protection. Slightly increases weapon handling accuracy. Greatly reduces recoil and shock damage. ]
[ Survivor Pants (Tier 2): Provides leg protection. Greatly Increases mobility when running or dodging. Slightly reduces stamina drain during sprinting. ]
[ Survivor Boots (Tier 2): Provides foot protection. Greatly reduces fall damage. Slightly increases movement speed on uneven terrain. ]
[ Survivor Utility Belt (Tier 2): Provides waist protection. Slightly helps control satiety reduction. ]
Kai stared at the gear, impressed. It wasn’t flashy, but it was practical, exactly what a survivor needed.
He began equipping them piece by piece.
The helmet fit snugly, and the help also slid down with a faint click after putting the visor down.
The jacket was light yet firm, while its armor felt like it was truly made for him, as it was hugging his frame.
Soon, the gloves also tightened around his hands, giving him a secure grip.
’This really feels good... I can already tell that’s high-quality made.’
The pants and boots completed the lower half, and they were surely designed for endurance and mobility. Finally, the utility belt was strapped around his waist, ready to carry the tools of survival.
When he was done, Kai received the Set Bonus Effect!

[ Set Bonus (Tier 2 Survivor Gear - Full Set Equipped): Enhances overall survivability. Improves stamina recovery during rest. Reduces fatigue accumulation in prolonged battles. Provides better adaptation to harsh environments such as heat, cold, or toxic air. ]
Kai exhaled slowly. "Now this... this feels right."
As soon as he said this, he heard hurried footsteps echoing through the corridor.
He knew immediately that there was an emergency, and he felt a little nervous.
Thud...
As expected, a scout burst into the quarters area. He was breathless and pale.
"Leader Kai! Artilleries, massive ones! They are being prepared! Our shelter might get bombarded!"
"What?!" Kai exclaimed as he stood up.
Artillery fire meant devastation... Their walls, their defenses, none of it would hold against something like that!

Shock coursed through him as the grim reality sank in. They had fought Sentinels, from D-Grade to C-Grade... He was expecting that the number of enemy units would just increase... However, this was entirely different!
Against bombardment, there was no survival. He had to do something.
’We’re trapped... unless...’
Kai thought as he swiftly went to check the observation area to see what really was going on.

chapters.title: Chapter 49: The Artillery Targets
paragraphs: It didn’t take long before Kai confirmed the large artillery being arranged.
’So that’s the Artillery?’
Kai thought as he adjusted the periscope.
Through the narrow scope, he saw the artillery...

It was massive with angular constructs of steel, mounted on tracked platforms. He couldn’t really properly describe it, but he knew that it was definitely something that humans would have difficulty creating.

Their barrels were long and segmented... Furthermore, it seemed as if it had hydraulic arms that locked each weapon into firing position, while mechanical loaders fed shells the size of small vehicles into their chambers.
Perhaps, the closest description he could give to this artillery was that its appearance resembles a spider carrying a long-barreled cannon.
Nonetheless, the sight was enough to make him feel worried. These weren’t improvised weapons, they were purpose-built engines of destruction, designed to level shelters in minutes.
’What the heck is this level of difficulty? Isn’t this a bit too much?’

Kai couldn’t help but think that the system had an irrational understanding of difficulty level. There was simply no way that survivors like them with barely any skills they could use would be able to survive something like this.
Still, none of them could complain right now...
Kai and his team had already begun discussing Plan D, the dreaded evacuation protocol!
However, one of the scouts shouted... "Wait! The artillery turned! It isn’t aimed at us! There’s another battle nearby!"
"What?" Kai’s eyes lit up as he realized that the system seemed to be reasonable.
Relief rippled through the room, but it was short-lived. The realization that the bombardment was part of a larger conflict meant danger was still close.
In the meantime, outside the Haven-45, a group of people were fleeing from the Mech Siege that had devastated their own Shelter, Haven-15!
"This is bad..." Terrence muttered as he looked at the artilleries...
Like Kai and the others, he was a Foreign Survivor, transported from Earth into this apocalyptic scenario. He was already 40 years old and was previously working as a security guard in a bank...
When given the choice, he had selected A.I. Rebellion Apocalypse over the other options, Zombie Outbreak and Demon Invasion.
He believed it was the most "livable" scenario. Machines, after all, were dangerous but not so unpredictable as zombies that could have various mutations, and Demons that could possess superpowers.
The machines, on the other hand, followed logic, programming, and tactics. He thought he could adapt to this world.
At first, he was lucky. His starting point was Haven‐15, a shelter far stronger than he had initially thought.

Within his first three days, or beginner protection, Terrence learned how fortunate he was. The shelter housed three Augmented Humans. They were warriors enhanced not only by Gene Serums but also by mechanical modifications.
They were legends among the residents, capable of feats ordinary survivors could not dream of.
The presence of these three guardians gave Haven‐15 a sense of invincibility. No one worried about raids or Sentinels that would stumble upon their hidden base from time to time.
Terrence himself grew complacent, reassured by the false security. He also had a revolver in his hands, so he felt a little comfortable.
He had to admit that during beginner protection, he trained little, relying on the Augmented Humans to protect them... since even with his Talent, there wasn’t much he could do.
But complacency was a fatal mistake.
The Mech Siege that struck Haven‐15 was unlike anything Terrence had imagined. Even the residents of the shelter were surprised by the intensity of the enemy’s attacks!
The Sentinels came in waves, supported by artillery fire and mechanical hounds.
The three Augmented Humans fought valiantly, but the sheer power of the assault was several times greater than anything they had faced before.
Even if the Haven‐15 had numbers, over 200 survivors, only 40 could fight. The rest were civilians, untrained and terrified.
Including Terrence and seven other Foreign Survivors, their combat strength was pitiful. They had relied too heavily on the Augmented Humans, and now the problem could be felt!

Terrence fled with two other Foreign Survivors who trusted his judgment. They ran through burning streets, dodging falling debris, as artillery shells dropped in the distance. Luck was on their side since none of the shells struck them directly.
But the devastation was everywhere.

As they fled, Terrence glanced back and saw something unforgettable. One of the Augmented Humans, the strongest of the three, had pushed forward, charging toward the artillery positions. His movements were inhumanly fast, and his fist carried force that could destroy a Sentinel.
With every step, he tore through Sentinels, dismantling their formation.
’Is he going to-’

For a moment, Terrence believed the impossible, that this lone warrior might silence the artillery itself. And indeed, the Augmented Human reached the emplacements, forcing the machines to halt their bombardment.
But it wasn’t for long. The Sentinels swarmed him, dozens upon dozens, mechanical hands and plasma blades tore him into pieces!
Even augmented strength had limits...
It was a heartbreaking sight. The strongest protector Haven‐15 had ever known was gone...
Now, Terrence and his two companions had nowhere to go...
Aurora, who was only 18 years old and was a convenience store clerk back on Earth, and Jonas of the same age, who was also a construction worker, could only look at him with hope...
The reason he decided to save the two were because they were still too young..
"Let me use my Talent again..."

[ Pathfinder (Epic): Grants instinctive awareness of safer routes and concealed zones. Generates a subtle protective field that conceals a small group from detection, suppressing noise and heat signatures. Activation costs 30 Spirit Points and lasts for 5 minutes, but the effect immediately ends if disrupted. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 50: The Save
paragraphs: Terrence felt the drain of Spirit Points as his Pathfinder Talent activated.

Thirty points vanished in an instant, and the sensation left him weak. Unlike Kai and the others, Terrence had never consumed the golden liquid or anything close to a Gene Serum. Those precious resources had been reserved for the Augmented Humans, the ones who fought on the frontlines.
Because of that, Terrence’s reserves were pitiful. He had only 54 Spirit Points in total. He had 50 at the starting point, and 4 more points after leveling up twice.
’Tsk... This is just too much...’Terrence thought as he checked his status.
[ Spirit: 4/54 ]

It wasn’t even possible for him to use Pathfinder twice in a single day. Thankfully, during his time working as a guard in Haven‐15, he had been paid with Spirit Stimulants. They were essentially recovery potions, restoring 10 Spirit Points each. It wasn’t much, but it allowed him to activate his Talent again when needed, since natural recovery was painfully slow, only 1 Spirit Point per hour!
Thanks to this stimulant, he had managed to use Pathfinder a second time.
"It’s here..." Aurora whispered, as she felt the changes around them.
The noise of their footsteps dulled, their frantic breathing softened, and even the air seemed cooler.
The most important effect of Pathfinder was its ability to mask their heat signature. Their movements became harder to track unless the enemy had a direct line of sight.
Then, Terrence focused on the passive effect of his Talent. His instincts sharpened, pointing him toward a direction he would never have chosen on his own.
The garbage field.
’What?’

Terrence grimaced. The place was foul, a mountain of waste piled high over years of neglect. The stench was overwhelming, thick with rot and decay. Flies swarmed in clouds, cockroaches scuttled across broken cans, and the ground was slick with filth. Infection would be inevitable if they stayed too long.
But Pathfinder insisted. It didn’t speak directly to him but he was informed that safety lay there. They probably had to conceal themselves among the trash.
"Move!" Terrence urged, guiding Aurora and Jonas toward the stench.
They followed without hesitation. At this point, they had no idea what else to do but run. To them, Terrence’s Talent was salvation, even if it led into filth.
Back in Haven-15, chaos spread.

Survivors scattered in every direction as panic started shattering the unity of the shelter. Soon, two large groups rallied behind the remaining Augmented Humans, each trying to lead their followers away from the siege.
But the Sentinels were watching and following them...
Terrence prayed the enemy’s attention would continue to focus on those larger groups.
’Yes, please... get their attention. Buy us time.’It was cruel, but survival demanded cruelty. He wasn’t ready to die just yet.
Aurora glanced back, recalling the people who had sheltered her. "They’ll make it, right?"
Terrence didn’t answer. He couldn’t. He just pressed forward, forcing his legs to carry them deeper into the garbage field.
Unfortunately, Pathfinder’s concealment wasn’t perfect.
The Hounds had not given up. Five mechanical beasts spotted them and locked onto Terrence’s small group.
"Shit... They’re coming!"
Jonas cursed under his breath, gripping his metal pipe tighter. Aurora also clutched her hatchet, ready to fight if necessary.

On the other hand, Terrence’s revolver felt useless in his hand. They were only Level 3, barely stronger than civilians. Against five Hounds, their weapons were laughable unless they strike their weaknesses.
’They found us too quickly... We barely reached the garbage field.’Terrence frowned.
Pathfinder’s effect was good, but the machines had already seen their movements. Even if their heat signatures were hidden, it wasn’t enough.
"Just run!" Terrence shouted.
With the stench choking their lungs and swarms of flies clouding their vision, the three survivors plunged into the filth, praying Pathfinder’s guidance would be enough to keep them alive.
Behind them, the five Hounds gave chase.
These quadrupedal machines with glowing red optics weren’t slowed by the terrain. Each step was calculated. They weren’t making unnecessary movements, making it easier for them to reach their group.
"Keep running!" Terrence shouted again.
He had a revolver, but he knew it wouldn’t be enough, unless he hit his target perfectly.
’I have to shoot at point-blank range if needed...’
That way, he might be able to destroy their sensors or the red optics on their faces. It wouldn’t win the fight, but it could buy them time.
Soon, the three survivors reached the scrapyard. They moved between piles of twisted metal and broken machinery.
They even considered collapsing piles of waste to slow the Hounds, but the machines adapted instantly, splitting into two groups to cut them off.
They’re fast!
Jonas swung his pipe wildly, striking one who lunged at him.
Bam!
The blow barely dented its chassis.
Thankfully, aside from biting and tackling, the Hounds had no advanced weapons. After all, they were mostly used by Sentinels to track targets.
"Ha!" Aurora shouted as she hurled her hatchet. It was barely embedded into another Hound’s leg joint, but the machine kept moving, dragging itself forward, and the hatchet was also thrown off.
Terrence then got closer and fired his revolver.
Bang!
The Hound staggered as sparks flew from its head, but it didn’t fall. At this time, Terrenace had only a handful of bullets left.
"Terrence!" Aurora screamed, ducking as another Hound leapt at her.
Jonas shoved her aside, taking the brunt of the impact.
Bam!
The machine’s jaws snapped inches from his throat. Jonas wrestled with it, but the Hound was stronger.
Terrence dashed forward and fired again.
Bang!
The bullet pierced its optic. The Hound didn’t collapse, but it lost control!
Because of that, Jonas managed to push it away.
"That’s close!"
"Focus!" Terrence reminded.
Soon, the three Survivors backed up with their weapons, as the remaining Hounds began circling them. It was as if they had received an order to hold rather than attack.
’Did they realize my revolver can still be a threat?’Terrence thought, aiming at them. But the Hounds didn’t flinch or show signs of retreating!
They were cornered.
"This is it..." Jonas muttered with despair in his voice. He realized he wouldn’t even have the chance to make his own Talent bloom.
But something unexpected happened next!

sentences.text: Terrence felt the drain of Spirit Points as his Pathfinder Talent activated.
Thirty points vanished in an instant, and the sensation left him weak.
Unlike Kai and the others, Terrence had never consumed the golden liquid or anything close to a Gene Serum.
Those precious resources had been reserved for the Augmented Humans, the ones who fought on the frontlines.
Because of that, Terrence’s reserves were pitiful.
He had only 54 Spirit Points in total.
He had 50 at the starting point, and 4 more points after leveling up twice.
’Tsk...
This is just too much...’Terrence thought as he checked his status.
[ Spirit: 4/54 ]
It wasn’t even possible for him to use Pathfinder twice in a single day.
Thankfully, during his time working as a guard in Haven‐15, he had been paid with Spirit Stimulants.
They were essentially recovery potions, restoring 10 Spirit Points each.
It wasn’t much, but it allowed him to activate his Talent again when needed, since natural recovery was painfully slow, only 1 Spirit Point per hour!
Thanks to this stimulant, he had managed to use Pathfinder a second time.
"It’s here..." Aurora whispered, as she felt the changes around them.
The noise of their footsteps dulled, their frantic breathing softened, and even the air seemed cooler.
The most important effect of Pathfinder was its ability to mask their heat signature.
Their movements became harder to track unless the enemy had a direct line of sight.
Then, Terrence focused on the passive effect of his Talent.
His instincts sharpened, pointing him toward a direction he would never have chosen on his own.
The garbage field.
’What?’
Terrence grimaced.
The place was foul, a mountain of waste piled high over years of neglect.
The stench was overwhelming, thick with rot and decay.
Flies swarmed in clouds, cockroaches scuttled across broken cans, and the ground was slick with filth.
Infection would be inevitable if they stayed too long.
But Pathfinder insisted.
It didn’t speak directly to him but he was informed that safety lay there.
They probably had to conceal themselves among the trash.
"Move!" Terrence urged, guiding Aurora and Jonas toward the stench.
They followed without hesitation.
At this point, they had no idea what else to do but run.
To them, Terrence’s Talent was salvation, even if it led into filth.
Back in Haven-15, chaos spread.
Survivors scattered in every direction as panic started shattering the unity of the shelter.
Soon, two large groups rallied behind the remaining Augmented Humans, each trying to lead their followers away from the siege.
But the Sentinels were watching and following them...
Terrence prayed the enemy’s attention would continue to focus on those larger groups.
’Yes, please... get their attention.
Buy us time.’It was cruel, but survival demanded cruelty.
He wasn’t ready to die just yet.
Aurora glanced back, recalling the people who had sheltered her.
"They’ll make it, right?"
Terrence didn’t answer.
He couldn’t.
He just pressed forward, forcing his legs to carry them deeper into the garbage field.
Unfortunately, Pathfinder’s concealment wasn’t perfect.
The Hounds had not given up.
Five mechanical beasts spotted them and locked onto Terrence’s small group.
"Shit...
They’re coming!"
Jonas cursed under his breath, gripping his metal pipe tighter.
Aurora also clutched her hatchet, ready to fight if necessary.
On the other hand, Terrence’s revolver felt useless in his hand.
They were only Level 3, barely stronger than civilians.
Against five Hounds, their weapons were laughable unless they strike their weaknesses.
’They found us too quickly...
We barely reached the garbage field.’Terrence frowned.
Pathfinder’s effect was good, but the machines had already seen their movements.
Even if their heat signatures were hidden, it wasn’t enough.
"Just run!" Terrence shouted.
With the stench choking their lungs and swarms of flies clouding their vision, the three survivors plunged into the filth, praying Pathfinder’s guidance would be enough to keep them alive.
Behind them, the five Hounds gave chase.
These quadrupedal machines with glowing red optics weren’t slowed by the terrain.
Each step was calculated.
They weren’t making unnecessary movements, making it easier for them to reach their group.
"Keep running!" Terrence shouted again.
He had a revolver, but he knew it wouldn’t be enough, unless he hit his target perfectly.
’I have to shoot at point-blank range if needed...’
That way, he might be able to destroy their sensors or the red optics on their faces.
It wouldn’t win the fight, but it could buy them time.
